News.title: How war has literally come to Putin’s doorstep as Ukraine’s Black Sea blitz puts tyrant’s personal palaces in crosshairs
News.content:
UKRAINE has brought war to Vladimir Putin’s doorstep, dragging the tyrant’s personal palaces into the crosshairs in an explosive show of strength.

Kyiv’s Black Sea blitz has left smoke billowing into the sky over Putin’s secret hideouts in recent months while a fatal bombing in Moscow last weekend struck just one mile from the Kremlin.



The attacks are a “deliberate effort” by Ukraine to expose the horrors of war to the Russian people and their bloodthirsty leader, experts say.

Seven people were reportedly killed and 40 were injured when a Ukrainian UAV struck the shores of Arkhipo-Osipovka, near Putin’s secret Gelendzhik lair on Sunday.



Dramatic footage showed the drone hurtling towards tourists on the popular beach after being damaged by Putin’s defence gunners.

It is unclear what the drone was targeting – but Putin’s high-security palace is located just 27km along the coastline.

“Targeting a place that Putin is known to go to is an obvious tactic for for the Ukrainians”, Simon Diggins told The Sun.

The Kremlin leader is believed to be holed up in the £1billion clifftop mega-mansion, terrified of a Ukrainian drone strike or a coup from his own war- weary inner circle, reports say.



It comes just months after Ukraine blasted a Russian “shadow fleet” tanker in full view of the hideout – which is famously kitted out with high-tech underground bunkers.

Diggins said: “Until this year the war has been something going on at a distance.

“Ukrainians have suffered significant numbers of shortages throughout the country.

“But the Russian people have been very largely kept immune to it.”

The strikes are part of a broad operation by Ukraine to “bring home to the Russian people, what’s going on in their name”, Diggins said.



After “taking control of the Black Sea” and blitzing military sites, Kyiv has turned its crosshairs to locations of “iconic or psychological significance”.

Since mid-July, Ukraine has struck dozens of sites belonging to Wildberries – the country’s biggest e-commerce platform dubbed Russia’s Amazon.

This followed a genius campaign of targeting Russian oil hubs and transport links, to paralyse Putin’s regime and spark fuel shortages.



Ukraine’s strikes deep inside Russia are part of a wider effort to push Moscow to the negotiation table and end the fighting.

And on Sunday night Volodymyr Zelensky’s forces hit their invader with what is believed to be its most intense bombing campaign of the war so far.

In Belgorod, just 30 kilometres from Russia’s border with Ukraine, a drone factory was targeted.

Elsewhere, two major oil refineries, Saratov and Ufa, and a Wildberries base at Novosemeykino in Samara region were also hit.

Additionally over Monday night, Ukraine struck a Wildberries hub in Chekhov, Moscow Oblast, just 40 miles south of the Kremlin.



At least five people died and six others were injured, local authorities said.

The wide-ranging strikes have suffocated Russian trade and fuel supply, with oil refining production slashed by 150,000 barrels per day in the last month.

In July, Moscow’s oil refining fell to 3.6 million barrels per day – the lowest rate since 2002, according to Bloomberg.



International security expert, Natia Seskuria, said: “Moscow has been targeted more often so far in 2026 than throughout all of 2025.

“By using domestic drone production to sustain deep strikes, Kyiv can hit targets far inside Russia, compel the Kremlin to spend more on air defense and emergency response, and make the war feel less distant to Russian society.

“These strikes are a deliberate effort to raise the economic and political cost of the war.”



If Kyiv maintains pressure, Ukraine will “inflict significant economic and reputational damage to Russia”.

“This is directly undermining Putin’s domestic narrative that he is in control of the situation and winning the war against Ukraine”, Natia said.

Geopolitical analyst, Jason Jay Smart, told The Sun: “Ukraine’s attacks are fundamentally changing the way that Russia operates as a state.

“This is changing how they can calculate how much money they’re going to have in their budget.

“That means how they can finance a war, how they will have logistics to continue this war.



“But also it’s bringing the war so common citizens see that though they are not being targeted, they see their government is not able to win this war.

“That this war is a total loss, and the longer it continues, the more they’ll suffer.”

The strain on Putin’s weakening war machine has backed the dictator into a corner.

Kremlin Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said the country is enduring a “very difficult period”, and Putin recently made the rare admission that the country is “struggling” with an energy crisis.

Dwindling manpower has seen Moscow deploy 30,000 North Korean troops and parliament allow even the most hardened criminals to be drafted.



Russia has suffered 1.4 million casualties since invading Ukraine in 2022, including an estimated 500,000 deaths.

Eastern European security expert Dr Richard Arnold previously told The Sun: “Russia is facing a manpower problem, simply because it hasn’t got enough people to power its industries and fight the war in Ukraine.”

A report last month showed that the average life expectancy for Russian troops on the frontline was just 20 minutes.

It also comes after a suicide bomber set off a homemade explosive device at an elite Moscow restaurant over the weekend.

The deadly blast ripped through the high-end Italian restaurant Balzi Rossi, killing five just 1.5 miles from the Kremlin.

Colonel-General Alexander Chayko was celebrating his birthday with high-ranking military officers, politicians and top bureaucrats when the homemade explosive detonated.

News.title: Mega-dinghy ‘carrying 160 migrants’ catches fire while attempting to cross the Channel
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

SMALL BOAT BLAZE Mega-dinghy ‘carrying 160 migrants’ catches fire while attempting to cross the Channel

A MEGA-dinghy believed to be carrying around 160 migrants caught fire during an attempt to cross the English Channel this morning.

The major search and rescue operation was launched at around 6am after the vessel’s engine burst into flames in French waters.



The Royal National Lifeboat Institution (RNLI) Eastbourne was deployed alongside British and French coastguard teams to help rescue those onboard and return them to France.

It is understood up to 160 people were aboard the overcrowded dinghy.



At this stage it is not yet known whether anyone was injured or killed in the incident.

A Coastguard spokesman said: “A vessel caught fire earlier this morning whilst in the French search and rescue region.



“UK vessels and a lifeboat are assisting.”

The incident comes as the number of migrants packed onto small boats crossing the Channel continues to rise.

The average number of people per boat has increased from just seven in 2018 to 63 in the year to March this year.

That figure rose to around 70 last month.



In July, a record 165 migrants crossed the Channel in a single dinghy, the highest number ever recorded on one small boat.

The Sun has contacted the French Coastguard and the Home Office for comment.

News.title: At least 17 migrants die trying to reach Majorca in small boat after 15 days adrift – as another vessel found near Ibiza
News.content:
BOAT OF DEATH At least 17 migrants die trying to reach Majorca in small boat after 15 days adrift – as another vessel found near Ibiza

AT least 17 migrants have died while trying to reach Majorca in a small boat after spending more than two weeks adrift, reports say.

The grim discovery was made just hours before another vessel carrying 15 North African people was located near the Spanish island of Ibiza.



The two reports come after some 70,000 migrants swam into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta from Morocco on Thursday.

Spanish authorities found the first small boat with two survivors inside in the early hours of Tuesday, about 12 miles southwest of Majorca.



The pair claimed they were part of a group of 17 other migrants who all died during the attempted crossing.

According to Europa Press, the two migrants told authorities they threw the 17 bodies into the sea.



The survivors were taken to Son Espases University Hospital, showing signs of malnutrition and dehydration.

Following the discovery, authorities scrambled a helicopter to locate any other migrants.

They also encouraged fishing or sailing boats in the area to report sightings.

Just two hours after the rescue near Majorca, a second boat was found 30 miles southwest of Ibiza.



The vessel was carrying fifteen people of North African origin when it was intercepted at 5:15am, the Civil Guard said.

It is currently unclear whether any of the survivors were injured.

This year, 211 boats carrying 3,935 undocumented migrants have arrived in the Balearic Islands, according to local authorities.

In 2025, 401 boats arrived at the archipelago with 7,321 people – marking an increase from data collected in 2024.



It comes after a huge wave of around 70,000 migrants entered the Spanish territory of Ceuta – located in Northern Africa – last week.

Over 48,000 have been frogmarched back across the frontier by Spanish cops and military personnel.

But there are currently an estimated 5,000 migrants, including nearly 1,000 children, remaining in the Spanish peninsula trying to dodge the security sweep.

Distressing pictures have shown dozens of North African youths sleeping on the pavement on makeshift beds made out of cardboard boxes.

News.title: Half of mums find breastfeeding harder than first expected – as a quarter admit they felt unprepared for it
News.content:
HIDDEN HARDSHIP Half of mums find breastfeeding harder than first expected – as a quarter admit they felt unprepared for it

THE top things mums wish they’d known before breastfeeding include how painful it can be, how hungry and thirsty it can make you and how difficult it can be outside the home.

A poll of 1,000 mums who have breastfed in the past three years found 24 per cent felt unprepared for the realities of it.



With leaking breasts, how lonely the experience can make you feel and how long feeds take among the biggest surprises.

But it’s not without positives, as 44 per cent said feeding led to a stronger bond with their child and 22 per cent felt empowered by it.



The research was commissioned by Momcozy, which has produced a report looking into breastfeeding in the UK in 2026.

Sophie Martin, author of The Infertile Midwife and lead midwife for an antenatal clinic, said: “There are lots of things mums wish they’d known about breastfeeding before having their baby.



“Many mums expect breastfeeding to come naturally, but the reality can be physically, emotionally and mentally demanding.

“At the same time, breastfeeding can bring an incredible sense of connection and confidence.



“It’s important that parents are given honest, balanced information so that they feel prepared both practically and emotionally for the realities of breastfeeding.

“Education and preparation is key.”

The report, released during World Breastfeeding Week, revealed only two per cent of mums expected to stop breastfeeding in the first month – but more than double actually did.

A wide range of experiences were reported, with 35 per cent breastfeeding for longer than planned, whereas 24 per cent stopped sooner than they hoped.

It emerged 54 per cent found breastfeeding harder than they expected, while 18 per cent believe it had a detrimental effect on their mental health.



Almost half (45 per cent) found feeding their newborn in public “difficult” – due to lack of privacy (65 per cent), feeling self-conscious (55 per cent) and receiving unwanted attention (53 per cent).

While 79 per cent said it affected their relationship with their partner, impacting intimacy (22 per cent), causing tension around night wakes (19 per cent) and feelings of resentment (18 per cent).

However, it also led to 19 per cent of couples working better together as a team and inspired 16 per cent of partners to find other ways to bond with their baby.

And the overwhelming majority (96 per cent) have experienced a “special moment” when feeding their new child.

The most special of these was seeing their newborn relax or fall asleep while feeding (47 per cent), followed by knowing they could comfort their child when they needed them (45 per cent).



Night feeds when everything felt calm (17 per cent) and the first-time feeding felt easier (14 per cent) are also cherished moments among those polled, data from OnePoll.com revealed.

But while 74 per cent of mums felt supported by their network during this stage of their baby’s life – just 11 per cent didn’t feel this way.

Tara Cai, head of user research at Momcozy, added: “The findings show while breastfeeding can be one of the most rewarding parts of early parenthood, it can also come with unexpected challenges that leave many mums feeling unprepared.

“But the results also highlight the importance of ensuring families have the resources, products and support networks they need to feel confident every step of the way.”

News.title: Inside ‘Britain’s strictest schools’ where pupils get detention for just looking out window & moving their pencil
News.content:
ONE of the strictest schools in Britain gives pupils detention for looking out the window and moving their pencil.

The Athena Learning Trust runs six schools in Cornwall and Devon, and has recently been forced to disband following allegations its discipline is too “oppressive”.



A BBC Panorama investigation found that some parents and students at Athena schools were unhappy with how strict the schools were.

At Athena schools, uniforms are inspected everyday, punctuality is strictly enforced and eyes must be focused on the teacher every time they talk.



The schools also have strict rules about when students can go to the toilet.

Around 6,500 pupils attend an Athena Learning Trust school in Devon and Cornwall, which says it’s trying to combat the historical educational disadvantage children in the south-west have faced.

In 2022, Athena took over Launceston College in Cornwall after Covid meant the school was struggling with enforcing children’s discipline.

Since then, the school’s grades for good maths and English have increased by five per cent, proof for some that this tough approach to learning works.



However, the tough rules, like keeping classrooms quiet, have meant music lessons are taught in near silence.

Estelle Pears, a former teacher at Launceston College said: “There’s discipline and there’s being oppressed.

It sounds dramatic but that’s what it became if you’re frightened of moving a pencil on a desk because you will get a sanction, if your eyes happen to flick out of the window for two minutes and you get a sanction.”



The Department for Education says on average about 20 per cent of a school day in English is lost to bad behaviour.

Athena schools enforce discipline with a two-strike policy with one breach of the rules leading to a warning, a second breach resulting in a detention.

The Trust calls detentions reflections, and from September 2025 to March 2026 pupils at Launceston College were being put on reflection around 1,000 times a month.

In reflection rooms, children have to work in silence for two lessons and a break, with some told to wear noise-cancelling headphones.

Athena Learning Trust said reflection rooms are “supervised environments where students continue learning independently”.



The Trust denied having a two strikes policy and that the “vast majority of students spend little or no time in these spaces”.

More than half of secondary schools in England use some kind of reflection room for detentions.

If the rules of reflection are broken, pupils can be suspended.

The Ilfracombe Academy in Devon was taken over by Athena almost three years ago and in that time suspensions have jumped to 1,000 a year – almost five times higher than the average in England.

The Trust told the BBC that suspensions are reserved for “serious or repeated breaches of behaviour expectations”.



Tom Bennett, a government advisor on behaviour in schools in England spoke generally about strictness in schools and says a strict school model is about the safety inside schools.

He said it’s important to instil in children that you can’t be “rude or cruel” to others.

“The benefit for schools to have this high level of strictness is that students understand really quickly that ‘this is what I’m expected to do’.

“And the joy of it is that the more students realise that they’ve got expectations with boundaries, the quicker they get into the habit of just doing it.”

But some parents have grown concerned that their SEND children are getting stuck in a cycle of being put in reflection and suspension as their learning needs are not being met.



The Athena Learning Trust said SEND children “are not routinely sanctioned for behaviours associated with their needs”.

More than 500 children have left Athena schools to be home schooled and many parents have complained to the school – but because it is an academy trust, this makes the complaints process lengthy and difficult.

However, the head of the Athena Learning Trust resigned after numerous protests by parents and the trust is now planning to disband.

Athena Learning Trust told the BBC that their schools are committed to “calm, safe, and purposeful” learning environments.

It added: “Teaching approaches are evidence-informed and do not replace or limit creativity, and consistent classroom routines and structured high-quality teaching are to support all students.”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The Department for Education said the allegations about Athena are “serious and concerning”.

It is “taking robust action to make sure the trust improves” and Athena now “subject to enhanced monitoring” to ensure “it’s approach to pupil behaviour is reasonable and proportionate”.

News.title: New wildfire evacuation order for Cali as hundreds of buildings razed to ground in Washington & cops make arson arrest
News.content:
A NEW wildfire has triggered evacuation concerns in California as firefighters battle another fast-moving blaze.

It comes as hundreds of buildings have already been destroyed in neighbouring Washington, where cops have now made an arson arrest.



The Gann Fire has ripped through at least 100 acres near New Hogan Lake in Calaveras County, with Cal Fire warning the blaze is racing uphill through grass and brush.

Extra firefighting resources have been called in as residents remain under an advisory and are urged to stay alert for further instructions.





Although no evacuation orders have been issued in California, the latest blaze comes as a far larger wildfire disaster continues to unfold in Washington state.

At least 700 homes, businesses and other structures have been destroyed in and around Spokane, Washington’s second-largest city, while around 67,000 people have been ordered to evacuate.

Read more on wildfires ROARING INFERNO Thousands evacuated as raging wildfires wipe out homes & spark explosions

Images from the disaster zone showed buildings engulfed in flames as thick black smoke billowed over neighbourhoods.

In many areas, homes were burned to the ground, leaving only chimneys standing among the smoking ruins.



Despite the widespread destruction, officials said there have so far been no reports of injuries or people unaccounted for, though they warned it remains early in the emergency response.

Patients at Spokane’s US Veterans Affairs hospital were among those forced to evacuate, while authorities opened a shelter at the city’s convention centre, where around 400 displaced residents were staying.

Firefighters continue to battle the three major blazes – the Old Trails Fire, Fairview Fire and Meadowview Fire – as dry conditions and powerful winds hamper efforts to bring them under control.

“We are not out of danger,” US Senator Maria Cantwell said during a news conference with federal, state and local officials.

“The next couple of days will be challenging.”



As the firefight continues, investigators announced a major breakthrough after arresting a man accused of starting the largest of the three fires.



Aaron F. Farinacci, 37, of Spokane, was arrested on Monday and booked on suspicion of first-degree arson in connection with the Old Trails Fire.

Authorities have not announced possible causes for the Fairview or Meadowview fires.

The Spokane County Sheriff’s Office said the investigation began after a community member reported seeing a nervous-looking man bent down beside the road near dry grass close to where the fire later erupted.

Farinacci was initially questioned and released, but detectives later reviewed body camera footage and reports before identifying him again and determining the fire had started where the witness had seen him.

Sheriff John Nowels said Farinacci allegedly had matches and a butane lighter when he was detained.



“As it happens in so many critical cases, it was citizens who were paying attention to their surroundings, being aware and willing to step up and say something that led to the relatively quick apprehension of Mr. Farinacci,” Nowels said.

Farinacci was due to make his first court appearance on Tuesday.

It was not immediately clear whether he had an attorney who could speak on his behalf.

Authorities said he has previously been convicted of felony manslaughter in Arizona.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The Spokane fires are among dozens of wildfires burning across the western US, stretching firefighting resources as dry weather, high winds and soaring temperatures continue to fuel dangerous conditions.

News.title: Migrants plan ANOTHER Ceuta invasion in days – after ‘convicted terrorists among thousands who stormed Spanish enclave’
News.content:
AFRICAN migrants are planning another invasion of Ceuta in just days – with online posts warning it may be their “last chance” to enter Europe.

Fears are also mounting convicted terrorists were among the tens of thousands of people who stormed the Spanish enclave last week, reports say.



Some 70,000 people swam from Morocco into the Spanish territory located in North Africa on Thursday.

But reports say the peninsula could see scenes of mayhem play out on the streets yet again, as plans are being made for another mass border crossing on August 15.



On social media, posts appear to be plotting another storming of the shores of Ceuta, with one message reading: “Everything will be seen that day.”

Another appears to call for the creation of a WhatsApp group, saying: “Our appointment is on 15/08/2026.”



Migrants desperate to try to reach Europe are reportedly being encouraged to join the group by sending a private message using the password “Ceuta”.

The revelation of the messages and posts – written in Darija, an Arabic dialect spoken in Morocco, Algeria, and Tunisia – has sparked major concern in Ceuta.



It also comes after Spanish cops claimed today at least a dozen convicted terrorists were among those who went across the border last week.

Terrorists previously deported to Morocco after arrests in Spain were part of the mass crossing, local outlet El Espanol reported.

Authorities believe it is “very possible” the number of criminals with links to Islamic extremists could increase.



The Spanish territory is still reeling from the “apocalyptic” scenes last week.

Up to 70,000 migrants were believed to have entered the city during the frenzied ordeal.

Over 48,000 have been frogmarched back across the frontier by Spanish cops and military personnel.

But there are currently an estimated 5,000 migrants, including nearly 1,000 children, remaining in the Spanish territory trying to dodge the security sweep.

Distressing pictures have shown dozens of North African youths sleeping on the pavement on makeshift beds made out of cardboard boxes.



The children will most likely end up being transferred to the Spanish mainland to ease overcrowding in Ceuta.

The city is already caring for some 850 children, but is planning to expand its facilities with two more centres as the number of youngsters is expected to rise over the coming days.

Fights broke out on Monday during the first Red Cross handout of food and drinks at Trampolin Beach.



Several police clashes also erupted last week amid the chaos, and at least 72 people were killed due to drowning or the resulting beach stampede after the migrants crossed into the Spanish territory.

Golden Owl, an Alicante-based tech startup, is among the organisations which have sounded warnings about the possibility of a new mass border breach in 11 days’ time.

It has linked 25 Facebook groups to the social media campaign that allegedly led to thousands of people joining the rush to reach Ceuta last week.



The start-up said: “This was not a spontaneous event.

“It was a coordinated, preplanned and publicised operation.”

Although it claimed there was no defined leader, it pointed the finger at a “small set of identifiable administrators and recruiters”.

This includes a man from the Moroccan city of Casablanca living in Istanbul.



The group also said the call for another storming of the beaches on August 15 was published on August 1.

It was made in a group with about 108,000 members and remains active, Golden Owl added.

Spanish PM Pedro Sanchez has blamed last week’s crisis on human smuggling mafias taking advantage of a recent Spanish Supreme Court ruling.

The decision banned summary returns of migrants intercepted in open water attempting to swim into Ceuta, or the other North African enclave of Melilla, 240 miles east.



Both territories endured days of chaos during the never-before-seen security breakdown.

Jaw-dropping footage showed swarms of people running up the shores of Ceuta and Melilla before pouring through the streets.

Terrified locals cowered in their homes as the streets turned into open toilets for hours in “apocalyptic” scenes.

Some migrants were heard shouting “Long live Spain!” as they dried off in the city.

Shocking reports claimed several locals suffered from attempted break-ins at their homes as footage captured multiple alleged incidents.



One showed a man climbing up a ladder as two others held it still around what appeared to be smashed glass from a first floor window.

A second seemingly showed dozens of migrants bundling into a small home and pushing through the tight entrance.

One Spanish business owner told RTVE: “It’s like an apocalypse. Waves of people everywhere.”

News.title: Derby Trans Pride 2026 set to make history as first Pride after UK single-sex toilet policy
News.content:
Derby Trans Pride 2026 set to make history as first Pride after UK single-sex toilet policy

As Derby Trans Pride celebrates its second year running, the annual event is set to make history as the first Pride to happen after the update EHRC rules take effect

View 2 Images Derby Trans Pride is set to make history

Derby's second annual Trans Pride is set to make history as the very first Pride to happen after Equality and Human Rights Commission (EHRC)’s new Code of Practice for Services takes effect.

‌



The new guidance from the Equality and Human Rights Commission (EHRC) confirmed that single-sex services must be based on biological sex, following a landmark Supreme Court ruling in April 2025.

‌



It addresses a variety of scenarios from sport, where it states trans people should compete alongside others of their birth sex rather than gender identity, to hospital wards, which it says can lawfully exclude trans patients if single-sex.

‌



The guidance also suggests it can be deemed legitimate, in limited circumstances, to ask someone to confirm what their sex is if “there is clear evidence of an issue with members of the opposite sex accessing or seeking to access the single or separate-sex service or association”.

View 2 Images Derby Trans Pride takes place this weekend

Traitors star backs conversion therapy ban after being told to 'repent' for being gay READ MORE :

The code takes effect on 5 August 2026, after Labour Equalities minister (and new party chair) Bridget Phillipson MP approved it — despite over 160 MPs called to reject it.

‌



Derby’s second annual Trans Pride will take place on Saturday 8 August 2026 from 2pm until 8pm at the Electric Daisy on Bold Lane, and will celebrate the trans, non-binary, intersex and gender-diverse community of Derby.

This year’s free event has speeches, drag performances, music, poetry and dancing, and stalls featuring everything from cookies and queer artists, to Derbyshire’s cornerstone LGBT+ support charity. After that, the revelry continues with an afterparty at Dubrek Studios, with DJs and performances (£3 plus booking fee, get your tickets here).

A march in support the trans+ community will take place at 3pm through the heart of Derby city centre, as a reminder that Pride is a protest.

Article continues below

A Derby Trans Pride spokesperson called out the UK's "plummeting in LGBTIQA+ rights", labelling it a "trans apartheid", referencing the UK drop from 1st, to 22nd in the ILGA-Europe ‘Rainbow Map’, a map which ranks 49 European countries on their respective legal and policy practices for LGBTI people.

They said: "That’s exactly why we needed a Trans Pride. Trans rights are the vanguard of the LGBTIQA+ community and the front line of human rights. Alongside protesting the negatives, we must also celebrate the joys of our vibrant community along with you all, and remind us we’ve always been here, why we’re still here, and what we can achieve together — we exist; we persist; and we resist. Happy Pride."

Derby Trans Pride takes place on Saturday 8 August 2026. Get your free tickets here.

News.title: Guatemala Fuego Volcano erupts live: Evacuation and nationwide 'danger' alert
News.content:
Volcán de Fuego in Guatemala - one of the most volatile volcanoes in the world - has started erupting, with a nationwide 'danger' alert issued

A state of emergency has been declared after the sudden eruption of one of Central America's most dangerous volcanoes.

Volcán de Fuego, famous for being one of the most active and volatile volcanoes in the world, started erupting in Guatemala on Monday morning and had intensified by nightfall, sending molten lava and huge plumes of ash and smoke spewing into the air.

Officials responded by issuing the country's second-highest emergency alert and rapidly moving to evacuate residents from the danger zone.

"An orange (danger) alert has been declared nationwide due to the eruption of the Fuego volcano,” Guatemalan disaster agency Conred posted on X as it began evacuating two villages close to the volcano's base.

News.title: Nigel Farage's Clacton by-election fight may cost taxpayers quarter of a million pounds
News.content:
Nigel Farage's Clacton by-election fight may cost taxpayers quarter of a million pounds

Reform chief Nigel Farage is facing comedy candidates including Count Binfance in next week’s Clacton by-election after major political rivals boycotted the contest

View 2 Images Nigel Farage’s Clacton by-election fight will cost taxpayers an estimated quarter of a million pounds, an official has suggested (Image: Getty Images)

Nigel Farage’s Clacton by-election fight will cost taxpayers an estimated quarter of a million pounds, an official has suggested.

‌



The Reform chief is facing comedy candidates including Count Binfance in next week’s vote after major political rivals boycotted the contest. They accused him last month of a political stunt last month for triggering the vote amid a Commons probe over a £5million gift received from a Thai-based crypto billionaire.

‌



Speaking to BBC Radio 4’s Today, chief executive of Tendering district council, Ian Davidson, said the ballot paper with 34 candidates was just under a metre long.

‌



He said: “We’ve got 34 candidates, which is the most number of candidates any parliamentary election has ever had. And the ballot paper is just under a metre a long. The cost of actually printing, running, and posting things like that is about four times the cost of the General Election where we had five candidates.”

Nigel Farage to face record 33 rivals in joke Clacton by-election despite mainstream parties boycott READ MORE :

View 2 Images Count Binface also stood in the Makerfield by-election, where Andy Burnham was victorious (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Asked about the cost of running the by-election, he said: “We don’t yet - we’re anticipating around a quarter of a million, about £250,000.

‌



“Most of that is paid by government, but not all. Tendering council will have to pay some of the cost because we’re having to put a lot of additional measures in place which are not what would be in the normal parliamentary by-election costs.”

He also said the council will not be using a stage to announce the results of the count - due to the sheer number of candidates.

When Mr Farage triggered the by-election last month, the Reform leader offered for his party to pay the cost of the contest but a Labour source dismissed the offer outright.

‌



They told The Mirror: “A political figure paying for a by-election he is standing in would clearly undermine the independence of the democratic process. It’s baffling that he can’t see that."

They added: “He cannot just buy his way out of the mess he’s got himself into. This by-election will be conducted along the same rules as all elections are in the UK. Farage will have to take responsibility for making taxpayers pay the cost of his latest ego trip.”

Mr Farage resigned as an MP after facing mounting pressure over his personal finances, including an undeclared £5million gift he received from Christopher Harborne shortly before the 2024 general election.

‌



He decided to throw in the towel to trigger a by-election in his seat, claiming that he would let the people of Clacton judge him, instead of the so-called establishment.

But all the major parties dismissed the plot as a desperate stunt and refused to stand candidates in the race.

Mr Farage's biggest rival is now Count Binface, the alter ego of Jonathan David Harvey, a British comedian, satirist and producer, who worked on hits like The Thick of It and Have I Got News For You.

Article continues below

He describes himself as an "intergalactic space warrior”, and the leader of the Recyclons from the planet Sigma IX. He claims to be over 5,900 years old, and has previously contested elections against Rishi Sunak, Andy Burnham and Boris Johnson.

Previously known as Lord Buckethead, he wrote on X: “Labour, Tories, Lib Dems and Greens: I demand you stand down in Clacton. I will be a unity candidate and pledge to build at least one affordable house.

“Nigel Farage says he wants The People versus the Establishment. So be it. Leave him to me.”

News.title: Only those with 'eyes of a sniper' can spot hidden cougar in optical illusion
News.content:
Only those with 'eyes of a sniper' can spot hidden cougar in optical illusion

If you think you have sharp eyesight, this tricky optical illusion will put it to the test. Hidden somewhere in the tall grass is a cougar - and only those with a keen eye can spot it in just 10 seconds

View 2 Images You must find the cougar hiding in the grass within 10 seconds (stock photo) (Image: Getty Images)

If you're on the lookout for a way to sharpen your problem-solving abilities, then this fiendishly tricky brainteaser could be exactly what you need. Keeping your brain fit and healthy is just as vital as regularly exercising the rest of your body - and it's far simpler to achieve than dragging yourself to the gym for a workout.

‌



The most effective way to train your brain is by challenging yourself with puzzles that force you to think differently. Doing this on a regular basis can improve cognitive function, lift your mood, enhance your problem-solving skills, and even help stimulate the areas of the brain that may be affected by conditions such as dementia. So if you're in need of a mental boost today, why not take on this challenging brainteaser?

‌



All you need to do is spot the cougar concealed among the tall grass - but you've only got 10 seconds to find it.

‌



Have a good look at the Reddit post. You'll notice a grassy area dotted with trees, rocks, and what appears to be a large hill in the background.

You might also spot the animal occupying a significant portion of the foreground - but we can tell you now that it isn't the cougar you're searching for!

View 2 Images Good luck! (Image: Getty Images)

‌



The user who originally posted the image on Reddit admitted they initially thought the animal at the front was the cougar, and had shared it as a joke.

But upon realising the real cougar was "actually pretty well hidden", they reposted it as a genuine challenge.

They wrote: "Posted this as a joke before realising that's not a cougar and the actual one is actually pretty well hidden."

‌



If you didn't manage to spot the cougar within the 10-second time limit, don't panic.

You might not be able to call yourself a genius or boast that you have the "eyes of a sniper", but it's still worth persevering until you track it down, however long that takes.

Cracking the puzzle - whether it requires 10 seconds or 10 minutes - will still give your brain a solid workout, and the more you practice, the quicker you'll become.

‌



And let's not forget the rush of dopamine you'll get when you finally nail it!

Found it yet? If not, we're about to reveal the answer below, so stop scrolling now.

‌



Answer

The cougar is extraordinarily well camouflaged, but it can be spotted on the right-hand side of the image.

Focus on where the animal in the foreground is positioned, and you should notice a large rock just behind its rear end.

Once you've located that, look just beyond it to discover the small face of the cougar gazing directly back at you.

Article continues below

The white markings around its mouth, eyes and ears are considerably easier to make out than the rest of the animal.

As numerous commenters pointed out, the cougar appears to have its gaze firmly fixed on the animal in the foreground - potentially sizing it up for its next meal.

One person said: "Cougar is locked in on some dinner." Another added: "Every time I see the cougar in one of these I say 'Oh no' out loud. They're so scary."

News.title: Heartbreak as 'cheeky' RNLI volunteer dies suddenly aged just 26
News.content:
Heartbreak as 'cheeky' RNLI volunteer dies suddenly aged just 26

The crew at Rhyl lifeboat station in North Wales is flying its flag at half mast to mark the passing of 'cheeky character' Kyle Simpson, who has died aged just 26

View Image RNLI lifeboat volunteer Kyle Simpson has sadly died (Image: WALES ONLINE)

An RNLI lifeboat station crew have paid tribute to one of their young volunteers who passed away aged just 26.

‌



Rhyl lifeboat station in North Wales said Kyle Simpson would be remembered for his "infectious laugh" and praised him for "going above and beyond what is expected of a new volunteer".

‌



The flag at the lifeboat station has been lowered to half mast to mark his passing, the station said. It added that while Kyle had only been at the station for a few months, his "cheeky character" had shone through, Wales Online reports.

‌



The RNLI station said: "It is with great sadness we report the sudden passing of Rhyl RNLI volunteer crew member Kyle Simpson.

Woman found dead in Liverpool hotel as two arrested on suspicion of murder READ MORE :

Budget airline grounds two flight routes from London Heathrow Airport READ MORE :

"Kyle had joined the station with the last intake of volunteer crew members, and like the rest of his cohort, he had been progressing well with his training, always being eager to learn and performing his shore crew role on multiple service calls.

"Although he had only been on the crew a few months Kyle's cheeky character shone through when he was at the station.

‌



"Over the past few months, Kyle had been going above and beyond what is expected of a new volunteer, and would spend a great deal of his time assisting with the maintenance of the lifeboat station and all its assets.

"Kyle also threw himself headfirst into the social aspect of the station, regularly attending fitness sessions and celebrations with the crew.

"We will greatly miss Kyle and his infectious laugh. We know he would have been a fantastic crew member who was already incredibly proud to be part of the team, and as a station, we were very proud to have him.

Article continues below

"The stations and the lifeboat memorials flags are currently at half mast in his memory."

RNLI Rhyl said its thoughts are with Kyle's family and friends at this "incredibly difficult time".

The UK office of the RNLI added: "We're so very sorry to hear about the sudden passing of Kyle. Thinking of the whole Rhyl crew and Kyle's family and friends at this incredibly difficult time."

News.title: Thousands of wasps take over home as man 'stung all the time' in horror infestation and is forced to flee
News.content:
Thousands of wasps take over home as man 'stung all the time' in horror infestation and is forced to flee

Craig McDonald said he had to leave his flat in Greenock, Scotland, due to a severe wasp infestation that has seen him and all his pets targeted by thousands of aggressive insects

View 5 Images Craig McDonald has been targeted by thousands of wasps (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

A man has been forced to repeatedly flee thousands of wasps after they infested his top-floor flat and descended on him, his dog and two cats in a relentless two-week assault.

‌



Craig McDonald, 38, said he and his pets have been "getting stung all the time" after the aggressive insects set up camp in the bedroom of his Greenock, Scotland home a fortnight ago. He is now unable to enter the room out of fear of being assaulted by the insects, causing a "serious impact" on his health and wellbeing.

‌



He has hit out at his landlord for failing to deal with the "nasty" situation, claiming they denied it couldn't possibly be a wasp's nest due to the time of year - despite the country having just entered peak wasp season.

‌



British bees are under threat with double killer wiping them out READ MORE :

View 5 Images Craig McDonald has been left scared to enter his bedroom (Image: Greenock Telegraph/George Munro / SWNS)

Craig said Oak Tree Housing Association has failed to deal with the wasp nest in the roof space or get rid of the insects, and fears he may have to leave his home altogether until the infestation is cleared. He has been increasingly worried about the health impact they are having, as their bedroom takeover means he hasn't "had a decent sleep in 10 days".

Craig said: "This is having a serious impact on my health. I am worried about my dogs and my cat. I have not had a decent sleep in 10 days. I can’t get to my bed. We are getting stung all the time. It is nasty.

‌



"I had contacted Oak Tree and they told me it couldn’t be a wasps’ nest because of the time of year. Then they sent in pest control. The guy was spraying something on to the roof. But then he went and put on all his protective gear, while I was standing in a pair of trousers, and asked me to help plug the gaps."

View 5 Images Wasps have made their home in Craig's house during peak season for the insects (Image: Greenock Telegraph/George Munro / SWNS)

"It made no difference, and the nest is still there. I need rid of it. I asked environmental health to come to my flat but they said I had to contact Oak Tree."

‌



The swarm of wasps took over the bedroom after getting through cracks in the ceiling. Craig said: "My neighbour was concerned about something in the loft. We spoke to Oak Tree but they said it was more likely to be rare bats, so leave them alone. Then I ended up with wasps in my bedroom."

The infestation has taken root during peak wasp season, with pest controllers noting that the insects manufacture their nests and multiply between April and October.

View 5 Images Craig said his landlords have not been able to help (Image: Greenock Telegraph/George Munro / SWNS)

‌



During that time, numbers of the pest tend to rise exponentially between June and July and peak in August, before dropping when temperatures cool. Wasps are also spurred by heatwave conditions, as they're more active when the weather is warmer, and they can use the sunlight to boost their movement.

Craig said that Oak Tree had contacted him to send pest control to his home again, but he warned them he would not be in, as he had been forced to leave for a period.

He added: "I needed a break, so I went to my mum’s, and I told Oak Tree this. I told them to send someone the day after, and I would arrange to be in. They need to do something."

Article continues below

View 5 Images Craig said he has decided to leave his flat due to the persistent problem (Image: Greenock Telegraph/George Munro / SWNS)

"I cannot live in here. It is a health hazard. I am in agony from the stings. It is horrendous. I am worried about my pets. I am trying to protect them because they don’t know what is happening to them."

In response, Oak Tree Housing said: "We are aware of the issue raised by Mr McDonald and are dealing with him directly with a view to resolving the matter as quickly as possible. As this concerns an individual tenant and his home, it would not be appropriate for us to comment further on the details of the case."

News.title: Beach trip left swimmer with parasite and in hospital for a month after 'swallowing contaminated seawater'
News.content:
Beach trip left swimmer with parasite and in hospital for a month after 'swallowing contaminated seawater'

EXCLUSIVE: Ex-tattoo artist Katherine Hopkins revealed she started experiencing agonising stomach cramps and had to use the toilet as much as 30 times a day after she took a dip during a heatwave

Woman hospitalised with cryptosporidium parasite after swimming in the sea near Brighton

A beachgoer claimed she was left violently ill with a parasite after taking a dip during the heatwave after "swallowing contaminated seawater."

‌



Katherine Hopkins was hospitalised for a month just days after she enjoyed a swim in the sea at Hove Lawns, Brighton, East Sussex. The 35-year-old swam in the water for four consecutive days from May 23, as well as enjoying one quick dip in Lancing Beach in West Sussex.

‌



Ex-tattoo artist Katherine said she was swimming for "three to four hours at a time" and did splash her face with seawater, but didn't ever put her head beneath the water. About 10 days after her first beach swim, Katherine began experiencing agonising stomach cramps - and had to use the toilet as much as 30 times a day.

‌



As her symptoms got worse, Katherine decided to go to hospital where tests revealed that Katherine had contracted cryptosporidium - a microscopic, single-celled parasite that causes an intestinal illness called cryptosporidiosis. Katherine, who was a particularly vulnerable patient after undergoing a kidney transplant in 2010, believes she ingested the parasite by swallowing seawater when splashing her face - which she fears could have been contaminated.

Following a month in hospital, Katherine was discharged home two-and-a-half stone lighter after surviving on a liquid diet. Katherine, who is still experiencing symptoms now, believes she got the infection from dirty seawater and fears more people could fall ill if they swim in it.

View 5 Images Katherine said she started to feel unwell after taking a dip in the sea (Image: Kennedy News and Media)

‌



New compensation rules for water firms who fail customers - what it means for you READ MORE :

Earlier this month, Southern Water was fined £7.1m at Canterbury Crown Court after repeated illegal sewage pollution incidents forced the closure of beaches off the Kent coast. The court heard how preventable equipment failures and poor operational oversight led to repeated discharges of untreated sewage between 2019 and 2021, some at the height of summer.

The prosecution comes almost exactly five years after Southern Water received a record £90 million fine for nearly 7,000 illegal sewage discharges across Hampshire, Kent and Sussex. Across five major pollution incidents, Southern Water repeatedly failed to maintain critical pumping equipment, delayed reporting pollution to regulators and allowed untreated sewage to enter coastal waters, the court heard.

Southern Water said that the incidents were five years ago, and pointed out that Hove's bathing water is now rated 'Excellent' by the Environment Agency. Katherine, who lives in Hove, East Sussex, said: "I went in the sea for the majority of each day. I loved it.

‌



View 5 Images Katherine said there were no signs saying "don't swim here" (Image: Kennedy News and Media)

"It didn't look visibly dirty. Brighton sea always looks a bit murky. There were no signs saying 'don't swim here'. There were kids in the water. I splashed my face and got water in my eye. I was in and out between three to four hours at a time."

But around 10 days after her first swim, she developed stomach cramps. Katherine said: "I was going to the toilet 20 to 30 times and I was so dehydrated. When I tried to drink water, it would just come straight out.

‌



"I was nearly fainting, I was hot and feverish. I threw up once. I thought I had food poisoning but I hadn't eaten anything to cause that. I genuinely thought I was going to die. I just felt really helpless."

After her symptoms failed to improve, Katherine went to Royal Sussex County Hospital in Brighton on June 16 where tests revealed she had contracted a parasite known as cryptosporidium that causes the diarrheal disease cryptosporidiosis.

View 5 Images Katherine Hopkins started to feel ill 10 days after she went to the beach (Image: Kennedy News and Media)

‌



Symptoms of cryptosporidiosis generally begin two to 10 days after infection, which Katherine says a specialist doctor suggested was likely picked up from swimming in the sea. The parasite lives intestines of infected humans and animals and then excreted out, often then being caught by people who come into contact with contaminated water sources.

It can enter the water from agricultural run-off via streams and rivers, storm overflows or from sewage discharges. In 2024, a cryptosporidiosis outbreak in Brixham, Devon, resulted in a utility company being fined £1.85million after hundreds of people fell ill and thousands had to boil their drinking water.

After a month in hospital, Katherine was discharged home on July 6 - and has vowed never to swim in British waters again. Katherine said: "I was really angry. I'm never going swimming in the sea in the UK again.

‌



View 5 Images Katherine was told she contracted the parasite cryptosporidium (Image: Kennedy News and Media)

"I think the beach should be shut off - there were so many kids swimming in there and god forbid if they were to get this. I was really shocked - I never thought I'd go in the sea and contract a parasite. People should be able to go in the sea without getting ill."

Adur District Council, who manage Lancing Beach, said that it was a matter for the Environment Agency. An Environment Agency spokesperson said: "Our seas, rivers and lakes naturally contain bacteria, some of which can cause illness. Additional bacteria can enter from farm runoff, sewage works and storm overflows, especially after heavy rain.

‌



"This bathing water is regularly monitored, and, on this occasion, there were no signs of any impact on water quality. We encourage people to follow UKHSA swimming advice and check Swimfo before visiting a designated bathing water."

Southern Water said there were no storm overflow released at either of the nearest locations during the times Katherine swam.

A spokesperson from Southern Water said: "Hove’s bathing water is rated 'Excellent' by the Environment Agency, with the nearest storm overflow more than two miles offshore and five miles north west of Hove.

‌



View 5 Images Katherine became violently ill after she swallowed contaminated water (Image: Kennedy News and Media)

"Local waters are further protected by Brighton’s super-sewer, which can store 150,000 tonnes of rainwater and wastewater for treatment at Peacehaven. No overflow took place on the days in question and samples taken by the EA on the 15th, 21st and 27th May showed no so-called faecal indicators.

"We are sorry to hear someone became unwell after swimming. Southern Water is committed to protecting bathing water quality and works alongside local authorities and other partners to safeguard our coastline."

Article continues below

Regarding the £7.1million fine for sewage pollution, Southern Water said it was 'deeply sorry' but pointed out the events took place between 2019-21. They admitted pollution incidents are 'unacceptable' but that since then they have made significant changes.

News.title: 'I wanted to throw my newborn on the floor - I feared I'd end up in prison or worse'
News.content:
'I wanted to throw my newborn on the floor - I feared I'd end up in prison or worse'

SENSITIVE CONTENT. EXCLUSIVE: Steve Sharman had no idea what was happening when he began experiencing postnatal depression following the birth of his daughter, leaving him contemplating suicide

Father with post natal depression feared he might 'hurt' his newborn daughter

The sound of his newborn daughter crying filled him with a rage so overwhelming he feared he might hurt her. While postnatal depression is commonly associated with mothers, research suggests it affects up to one in 10 new fathers.

‌



For 35-year-old Steve Sharman, from Stoke-on-Trent, it all began when his daughter, Florence, came home from the hospital in August 2023 following a traumatic birth. Her crying triggered intense, terrifying, emotions he had never experienced before.

‌



"I've never been an angry person," Steve says. "But I felt this overwhelming anger. I wanted to throw her on the floor, scream at her, harm her. I never acted on those thoughts, but they were so strong. It felt like I was becoming someone else."

‌



View 7 Images Steve initially felt embarrassed to ask for help (Image: Supplied)

Despite affecting hundreds of thousands of families, many men suffer in silence due to ongoing societal expectations and a lack of support following birth. For Steve, who had never previously struggled with his mental health, the illness came out of the blue.

"It was the worst day of my life but also the best," he recalls.

‌



7 View 7 Images Florence is Steve and Emily's first child (Image: Supplied) 7 View 7 Images Steve felt overwhelming anger when Florence cried (Image: Supplied)

His wife, Emily, endured an 18-hour labour before doctors performed an emergency caesarean section. Although Florence was born healthy, there were concerns about her heart, keeping the family in hospital for five days.

‌



The trauma, however, didn't end when they were discharged.

"When we brought her home on our wedding anniversary, everything changed," Steve says. "It was the crying that triggered something in me."

Alongside explosive anger came crushing depression. "I felt completely useless to the world. I'd lock myself away in the spare room and not want to do anything," Steve says. "I had moments where I contemplated suicide. I genuinely thought the worst-case scenario was I'd either end up in prison or end my own life."

‌



Steve hid what he was experiencing from everyone around him.

"I masked it all. I was good at pretending parenthood was a dream. A lot of the time it was lovely, but this darkness was always hovering."

Like many new fathers, he felt pressure to remain the family anchor, especially when he returned to work as a Communications Officer in the NHS just four weeks later.

‌



"As a dad you're seen as the man of the family - the one who's supposed to keep everything together."

Dr Anna Machin, author of The Life of Dad, says that social expectations are a primary reason reasons men fail to seek help.

"We expect men to step into the role of supporter and emotional rock which means that they should negate their needs and feelings to support their partner," she explains.

‌



"Many won't speak to their partner about their mental health because they don't want to burden her further."

Male postnatal depression often manifests differently than in women.

7 View 7 Images Emily has been a 'rock' for husband Steve (Image: Supplied) 7 View 7 Images Florence is now nearly three years old (Image: Supplied)

‌



"Men tend to show less obvious low mood but much higher anxiety, anger, irritation and frustration. They're also more likely to withdraw from family life or self-medicate with alcohol or drugs."

Biological factors also play a role, a new father's testosterone levels can drop by up to 30 percent. Because higher testosterone appears to protect against depression, this hormonal shift can increase vulnerability during an already intense transition.

The sudden rages frightened Steve more than anything else.

‌



"There was one time Emily was unpacking the car and Florence had a meltdown. I screamed in her face. My wife wasn't scared to leave Florence with me, but she was worried about both of us."

On another occasion, overwhelmed by the crying, Steve got in his car to pick up his brother from the station.

"I have absolutely no recollection of the journey," he admits. "When I got to him, I just broke down. He was the first person I told."

‌



Eventually, Steve forced himself to see a GP.

"I nearly walked out of the waiting room because I didn't think I deserved help."

Instead, he was prescribed antidepressants and referred for NHS talking therapy. His wife Emily, a critical care nurse, stood by him throughout - though Steve admits the strain tested their marriage to its limits.

‌



"Before Florence was born, we'd assumed if either of us developed depression it would be Emily because she went through pregnancy and birth. Instead, she was my rock."

The experience also challenged assumptions Steve himself had held.

7 View 7 Images Steve now helps other dads working through their emotions (Image: Supplied) 7 View 7 Images PANDAS played a huge role in Steve opening up to others (Image: Supplied)

‌



"It was completely brand new for me. I'd never had mental health problems before, so I understand why people don't ask for help."

Although therapy improved his symptoms, it took almost a year before Steve fully accepted what he had experienced.

The true turning point came four months after Florence was born, when Steve's sister-in-law suggested he contact the charity PANDAS, a charity supporting families affected by perinatal mental illness.

‌



"I joined one of their Zoom calls for dads. I was actually the only dad on there, but I shared my story and, for the first time, someone told me what I was experiencing was normal.

"They shared experiences that were almost identical to mine. When the call ended, I burst into tears because it was the first time I didn't feel broken."

With PANDAS encouragement, Steve wrote a letter to his parents opening up about his struggles and suicidal thoughts. He later shared his story publicly on social media to break the stigma.

‌



"It was incredibly difficult admitting I'd had suicidal thoughts, but it lifted such a weight."

Dr Machin says stories like Steve's are critical because many fathers never realise what they're experiencing has a name.

"There is currently no routine screening programme or diagnostic tool for perinatal depression in men, unlike the support pathways that often exist for mothers," she says.

‌



"That means many fathers simply fall through the cracks."

Elliott Rae, founder of Parenting Out Loud, says workspaces also need to step up to support men after having children.

He told the Mirror: "It's really important dads have time to adjust to the massive life change of having a baby," he explains. "Many dads go through emotional and hormonal changes, including a drop in testosterone which can affect their mental health.

‌



"One of the key risk factors for dads experiencing postnatal depression is not bonding with their baby. If the dad goes back to work too soon, the baby cries when they are picked up, they don't feel as confident with the baby independently. We know that can be one of the key risk factors for dads developing postnatal depression because he doesn't feel he's growing into the role of a father or building a relationship with his child."

Today, three years after Florence's birth, life looks very different for Steve and his family.

Florence is thriving, and toddler meltdowns no longer overwhelm him.

‌



"I've got that understanding now. It doesn't faze me anymore."

The couple is even discussing having a second child.

"It hasn't put us off. I can't predict how I'll feel, but now I know what happened to me and I know I would ask for help much sooner."

‌



Steve now volunteers with PANDAS, speaking on podcasts, contributing to research and delivering talks to healthcare professionals.

"If my story helps just one person, then it's worth it," he says.

"I want dads to know there is absolutely no shame in speaking up. Looking back, I'm actually proud of how I got through it."

Article continues below

For emotional support you can call the Samaritans 24-hour helpline on 116 123, email jo@samaritans.org , visit a Samaritans branch in person or go to the Samaritans website.

News.title: Breast cancer checks missing most women under 50 who are at risk, says study
News.content:
Breast cancer is a leading cause of death in women under 50 in the UK.

About one in seven women develops breast cancer in their lifetime, yet only 5-10% of cases are linked to inherited genes.

Most cases - 96% - are in women over 40, while 25% are in women over 75.

Men can get breast cancer too, with about 420 new cases every year in the UK.

In England, guidance from Nice recommends GPs ask about family history if a woman is worried that she might have a higher risk of breast cancer, and sometimes if they are over 35 and using an oral contraceptive pill or considering taking hormone replacement therapy (HRT).

Hormones have been linked to a slightly increased risk of breast cancer, although larger risk factors include alcohol intake and obesity.

The study, by a team from Cambridge University and the Institute of Cancer Research, looks at how to predict breast cancer risk in younger women.

They used a risk calculator called Boadicea that combines factors such as family history, lifestyle, reproductive history and genetic information to give a risk score.

If all women under 50 were to have this done, they estimate about a quarter (26.5%) would be categorised as at above-average risk and referred for further assessment.

This would include a third of women under 50 (34.8%) who develop breast cancer within 10 years.

By comparison, the current Nice criteria would result in 1.4% of women under 50 being referred for further assessment, which would include just 4.4% of those women who develop breast cancer.

A main reason for the disparity, the researchers say, is because three-quarters of women (73%) under 50 who develop breast cancer within a decade have no family history of breast cancer - the key criterion in the Nice guidelines.

News.title: There's a reason child vaccination rates are falling - and it's not social media
News.content:
Twenty-week-old Grayson easily could have become one of the tens of thousands of British babies left unvaccinated against polio.

His mother, Lily, agrees with the principle of immunisation. But overwhelmed by the early weeks of motherhood, and suffering from post-partum depression after a traumatic birth, she was daunted by the prospect of a long journey to a doctor's surgery. "I've been through the trenches, awake all night. You don't want to leave the house, or go to a different town."

Weeks ticked by, and eventually Grayson missed the polio and diphtheria jabs he was supposed to get at eight weeks old. By that point he was officially classed by the NHS as "overdue" for vaccination; effectively, he was on his GP's naughty list.

Then Lily realised there was a clinic practically on her doorstep - at a location she hadn't expected.

That clinic - in Keighley, west Yorkshire - runs from a vacant retail unit at the Airedale shopping centre, a 1960s-era precinct that locals say has fallen on hard times in recent years, with plenty of empty, boarded-up units. The staff who created the clinic thought: why not use one of those vacant units to administer vaccines?

"This was an empty shop; there was nothing here, the windows were all blacked out," Flora Jennings, a local charity coordinator, tells me over the sound of a baby's laughter, on the morning I visit the clinic.

News.content:

News.title: Ariana Grande says decision to step back 'was not reactive or impulsive'
News.content:
Ariana Grande has spoken for the first time since her publicist announced over the weekend that the singer would be "taking a step back from visibility" once her current tour ends next month.

Grande returned to the stage on Monday evening in Chicago for another stop on her Eternal Sunshine Tour, telling fans, external: "The announcement that was made yesterday was not a reactive or impulsive thing. It is something that I had decided to plan... quietly, a long time ago."
