Sports.title: Champions League stadium to look unrecognisable as £171m renovation of 54,732-seater arena is approved
Sports.content:
NAPOLI are set to give the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona a mega-money makeover.

The Serie A giants, who are eyeing a summer move for Chelsea defender Benoit Badiashile, have had major redevelopment plans approved.



It comes after Chelsea fans highlighted safety issues when they headed to Napoli in the Champions League last season.

And the Italian heavyweights’ 54,732-seater home will look unrecognisable after the £171million renovation is complete.



The athletics track separating the action from the raucous fans is set to be ditched as part of the proposal.

Napoli, who bagged their fourth Serie A crown last year, also want to extend the second tier and have the seating just seven metres from the edge of the pitch.



The third tier will also be reopened after being off limits to supporters due to safety concerns.

Structural vibrations could be felt when fans were celebrating, leading to changes needing to be made.

But having fans back in those areas could allow the capacity at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona – which was renamed in honour of the Argentine legend in 2020 – to increase to in the region of 65,000.

Initial preparatory work has already begun and is expected to move into a more advanced stage in the autumn.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

But Napoli, fresh from seeing Antonio Conte quit as their boss at the end of last term, are desperate not to stray too far from how the arena looked when it first opened in 1959.

The eye-catching renovation, which includes new VIP boxes and hospitality areas, is on course to take place in stages.

It means Napoli, who are preparing for another season of Champions League action, will not have to leave their home while upgrades are made.

And the project was given the green light after a proposal was submitted by Mayor Gaetano Manfredi and infrastructure councillor Edoardo Cosenza.



The majority of the building work is expected to get underway after Italian host cities for Euro 2032 have been selected.

But city and regional authorities insist Stadio Diego Armando Maradona will be revamped even if it is not in line to stage showdowns during the tournament.

Sports.title: Jadon Sancho's Man Utd decline and manager trend leaves unwanted star in awkward spot
Sports.content:
It was seen as such a flex by those at Manchester United that, when Jadon Sancho returned to the north west, he chose them given his prior association with Manchester City.

The winger moved to the Etihad as a teenager and continued his development in their youth ranks but, despite being highly rated, opportunities weren't as forthcoming as he'd like and he chose to leave for Borussia Dortmund.

Rather than pursue the path taken by Phil Foden, one of patience, Sancho decided the time was now and for several years he looked to have nailed his decision. The Englishman thrived in Germany off the back of regular starts, impressing enough to become part of the Three Lions set-up.

The clamour for his signature was real and after scoring 16 times in his final year with Dortmund he would choose the red side of Manchester. Dortmund banked £72million and the next step in a career that had only been on an upward trajectory had people inside Old Trafford licking their lips.

‌



10th-tier side release bizarre Jadon Sancho statement as Man Utd flop looks for new club READ MORE :

7 transfers Man Utd need to complete for Michael Carrick to win silverware this season READ MORE :

In truth, his best football remained in Dortmund and, had it not been for a Brazilian named Antony, we may well be sat here discussing Sancho as the greatest transfer flop in United's history.

Imagine training with a team in the tenth tier of English football and them having to release a statement to confirm you're not actually signing with them. Obvious no? Well Flixton FC, of the North West Counties league, said on their social media: "To clarify, Jadon was not on trial with the club and was not involved in any transfer discussions."

If you wanted to know how dark things have got for Sancho, there's your answer.

View 4 Images Jadon Sancho has never been able to replicate the form he's shown at Borussia Dortmund (Image: Getty Images)

‌



The 26-year-old shouldn't even be in his peak years yet and still United allowed him to walk out of the door once his contract expired. Damning. Maybe even more damning is the lack of clubs wanting to snap him up for nothing.

The list of managers who have looked at Sancho and gone 'no thanks' is growing. Unai Emery at Aston Villa used him sporadically and opted against a permanent deal. Chelsea under Enzo Maresca went as far as to pay a penalty fee to avoid signing Sancho. And Erik ten Hag saw something he didn't like.

If you want to pinpoint a moment that really begun the demise then the public spat with the former United boss is likely it. Sancho was snubbed from the matchday squad that travelled to Arsenal in September 2023. Why?

"On his performance on training we didn't select him," said the Dutchman. "You have to reach the level every day at Manchester United. You can make choices in the front line, so in this game he wasn't selected."

‌



The worry for Sancho is Ten Hag was not some bitter manager who had inherited a player he didn't like, these were comments that had been made before. During his time in Germany Dortmund boss Lucien Favre admitting he needed to be hard on the winger and club chief Sebastian Kehl called out Sancho after returning late from international duty.

View 4 Images Erik ten Hag and Jadon Sancho fell out publicly (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

“Like every other player, he has to know that no matter how good you are, there are limits," he said. "There is a certain framework in which all players can move with us. Football is a team sport. You have to be consistent and make a tough decision in the interests of the group.”

Sancho would ultimately never recover from his spat with Ten Hag, which led to three loan spells away in as many years. His performances didn't exactly portray a player who was due some leeway from his manager either.

‌



In his first year at United, despite the fanfare surrounding his arrival, it took Sancho until late October to come up with a goal or an assist. He would score just three Premier League goals - the first of which came too late for Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, the man who signed him. He was sacked, but before receiving his marching orders claimed Sancho "will be a top player" after a poor start to his United career. That wasn't the only thing the Norwegian would prove to be wrong about during his time in Manchester.

Sancho once played in a Dortmund team that also included Jude Bellingham and Erling Haaland. Dortmund, for all their history, is something of a stepping stone club and bigger things were always in the reckoning for all three men. Bellingham and Haaland have gone on to win Champions Leagues and dominate the teams they joined next.

View 4 Images Jadon Sancho spent last year at Aston Villa, but they didn't want him permanently (Image: Getty Images)

Sancho's waning career owes to a poor decision over where to move, but equally his failure to fulfil his own potential is something he must own. He told Ten Hag that he'd been a "scapegoat" when the then manager called him out in public, but there's been no meteoric return to form once he got to play away from the Dutchman.

‌



There's been one occasion, back in 2024 when Sancho made a six month return to Dortmund on loan, that the Englishman looked like that player who had the footballing world in awe.

He was key in the German side's surprise run to the Champions League final, which included a win over PSG in Germany. On that night in April, on a pitch that included Kylian Mbappe and Ousmane Dembele, Sancho stood head and shoulders above the rest.

The plaudits came flying in, deservedly so, but that outing was a flicker of light in a career that is dimming as the seasons go on. Fast forward two years, and he's fishing in a market with no one biting.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso could hand five forgotten Chelsea players a fresh start
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso could hand five forgotten Chelsea players a fresh start

Xabi Alonso has been in charge at Chelsea for just over a month and several players will be aiming to force their way into contention under the new boss

View 5 Images Xabi Alonso has been running the rule over his Chelsea squad (Image: Brendon Thorne, Getty Images)

Chelsea are several weeks into the Xabi Alonso era and have already made additions to their squad under the new boss. However, the Spaniard's arrival could also present a route back into first team contention for some players who found themselves out of the picture under previous bosses.

‌



The Blues have already spent more than £300million on new signings, with more than one third of that coming from their British record deal for Morgan Rogers. Some new arrivals were agreed before Alonso's arrival - including a big-money move for Geovany Quenda - while the former Bayer Leverkusen chief has also added Premier League experience in the form of Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson.

‌



Money has been raised through the sales of Marc Cucurella, Andrey Santos and Tyrique George. More exits could yet follow as the new manager takes a proper look at his squad during pre-season.

‌



At the same time, though, the change in the dugout could open doors for players who thought there time might have been up this time last year. Here, we've taken a look at five stars who could yet get a chance to resurrect their Chelsea careers.

FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Alejandro Garnacho takes brutal swipe at Chelsea immediately after Aston Villa debut READ MORE :

Chelsea squad's immediate reaction to Mykhailo Mudryk bombshell and imminent return READ MORE :

Mykhailo Mudryk

Mykhailo Mudryk spent time on the sidelines as a result of a doping ban but his availability makes him a notable name on this list. The winger was initially dropped from the Chelsea squad in November 2024 following a provisional suspension imposed by the Football Association.

‌



The 25-year-old subsequently received the maximum four-year ban after an "adverse finding" for the prohibited substance meldonium during a routine test. Mudryk challenged the ruling at the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) and is now cleared to return to action after acknowledging he breached the regulations.

View 5 Images Mykhailo Mudryk is available again (Image: Darren Walsh, Chelsea FC via Getty Images)

Alonso said he is "very happy" to have the winger back in the fold but suggested a return might be a longer process given his time out of the game. The manager said: "It's too early to tell how he is in terms of fitness, in terms of the game time you need to be involved again, so it's still too early to tell.

‌



"But we are happy for him, especially for him, because we are probably not able to understand what he has been through during this time and how he feels at the moment with the things he has had to cope with."

Mudryk had already contributed 21 goals and assists across 73 outings for the Blues. He will be targeting even greater achievements upon his comeback, though there have already been reports that other clubs are ready to test the water over a transfer deal.

Mike Penders

Belgian goalkeeper Penders is yet to feature competitively for Chelsea but his standout loan spell at Strasbourg could herald a fresh chapter at Stamford Bridge. Robert Sanchez is expected to start the season as first-choice goalkeeper for the Blues, though Penders, 21, will be keeping close tabs from the sidelines.

‌



View 5 Images Mike Penders is back after his trip to the World Cup with Belgium (Image: Florencia Tan Jun, Getty Images)

Sanchez is also managing a minor knock during the Blues' pre-season tour. His younger colleague has now traveled to Hong Kong to gather invaluable experience in the lead-up to the new season.

During his temporary stint in France, Penders clocked up 52 appearances across all competitions. He registered 12 clean sheets, helping Strasbourg reach the semi-finals of the Conference League.

‌



The considerable experience accumulated in Ligue 1 will undoubtedly prove instrumental in Penders potentially securing a regular berth in Alonso's first-team plans. Now he has a chance to show the new boss what he can do.

Axel Disasi and Aaron Anselmino

Alonso has confirmed he wants "four or five" centre-halves at his disposal at Chelsea this season. This could pave the way for defensive pair Axel Disasi and Aaron Anselmino, both of whom have recently returned from loan stints.

View 5 Images Axel Disasi finished last season on loan at West Ham (Image: Rob Newell - CameraSport, CameraSport via Getty Images)

‌



Since his arrival in 2023, Disasi has been sent out on loan twice to Premier League rivals Aston Villa and West Ham. Anselmino joined a year later but has had three spells away, including stints at Borussia Dortmund, Boca Juniors and Strasbourg.

There are reportedly plans to facilitate departures for Trevoh Chalobah and Benoit Badiashile, with Mamadou Sarr also anticipated to head out on loan. This creates room in the centre-back department, with Maxence Lacroix, Levi Colwill, Wesley Fofana and Tosin Adarabioyo remaining at the club.

The question concerns whether Disasi or Anselmino would be prepared to begin the campaign as the fifth choice of five. There are reports of interest from the former, with West Ham still keen to convince him to return and help them push for promotion from the Championship.

‌



Liam Delap

View 5 Images Liam Delap struggled for consistency last season (Image: Eurasia Sport Images, Getty Images)

Liam Delap joined the Blues last summer but has endured a difficult time with injuries since touching down in west London. The 23-year-old missed a total of 83 days during his debut campaign for the Blues and only managed to string together a run of appearances from January onwards.

Nevertheless, Delap completed just three full 90-minute matches from that point. He struggled to deliver in front of goal but will now be desperate to demonstrate his value to Alonso.

‌



The Spaniard has commended the striker for his pre-season efforts, saying: "Every player that is involved is doing well, Liam as well. It was 60 minutes when he had to battle hard against the centre-backs, a good few lays off, so he's doing well and preparing for the season."

When quizzed on whether he believed Delap was struggling with his confidence, Alonso said: "I see him in a good mood, in a good desire to get proper fitness, proper football feeling good, and he's doing well."

Sports.title: Ex-Premier League star Yannick Bolasie hospitalised in Brazil after freak injury
Sports.content:
Ex-Premier League star Yannick Bolasie hospitalised in Brazil after freak injury

Yannick Bolasie now finds himself playing in Brazil but the ex-Premier League star suffered a nasty injury that has left him hospitalised

View 2 Images Yannick Bolasie was hospital with a bizarre injury

Former Crystal Palace and Everton star Yannick Bolasie has suffered a nasty pancreas injury following a scary pitch collision in Brazil.

‌



The 37-year-old was taken to hospital during Chapecoense’s Sunday Copa do Brasil clash against Cruzeiro after being caught by opposition player Kaique Kenji at the end of the first-half.

‌



Bolasie immediately went down and clutched his stomach as medics ran onto the pitch. The DR Congo international was able to walk off the pitch, but couldn't carry on and later was sent to hospital.

‌



It was then discovered he had suffered an injury to his pancreas and reports from Brazil claim he is set to spend several weeks in recovery. A full timeline for his return has not yet been set.

Arsenal star gives honest verdict on Vinicius Junior as transfer hinges on fresh talks READ MORE :

A statement, re-shared on his Instagram story, said: "Just a quick update to everyone who has been seeking news and wishing Bolasie well since yesterday: as everyone knows, yesterday he suffered a very strong impact to his rib area, resulting in his hospitalization.

"He is currently stable but will undergo further tests and remains under observation. Thank you all for your messages of support and well wishes. God willing, everything will be alright soon."

‌



Bolasie only moved to Chapecoense earlier this year as the winger plays out his final days in South America having spent the peak part of his career in England's top flight - capping an impressive rise that saw him start his playing days in non-league with Hillingdon Borough.

View 2 Images Yannick Bolasie is in the midst of his first year with Chapecoense

His most recent stint in English football saw him playing in the Championship with Swansea City, but he's spent the last three years in Brazil playing with several teams. His time in Europe saw him play for the likes of Anderlecht, Sporting Lisbon and Caykur Rizespor.

Article continues below

Bolasie arguably enjoyed his best days under Alan Pardew when he and the Eagles were enjoying a purple patch and the then manager claimed he would only sell his winger for £60million - that came in 2015 when such a fee would've been mouthwatering for a mid-table player.

Sports.title: Arsenal star gives honest verdict on Vinicius Junior as transfer hinges on fresh talks
Sports.content:
Arsenal star gives honest verdict on Vinicius Junior as transfer hinges on fresh talks

Arsenal spent more than £30m to land Christos Tzolis and the winger has talked up his ability as the Gunners consider landing Vinicius Jnr - which would ramp up competition in the final third

View 2 Images Vinicius Jr is locked in a contract standoff with Real Madrid (Image: NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Arsenal's new arrival Christos Tzolis is confident he can become a regular under Mikel Arteta despite the club's interest in Vinicius Junior.

‌



The Greece international became the team’s third signing of the summer when he made a £34million move from Club Brugge last month - but a blockbuster switch for Vinicius could impact on his future prospects at the Emirates.

‌



Tzolis has scored more than 20 goals for each of the last three seasons, doing so initially with German side Dusseldorf and then during his two years in Belgium.

‌



The 24-year-old has underlined his confidence in his own ability and insists, as and when he gets the opportunity to impress, he will put Arteta on notice as he bids to secure a starting spot at Arsenal.

Vinicius Jr to Arsenal transfer hint as key figure flies into London READ MORE :

Bruno Guimaraes to Arsenal saga has Newcastle in contention for all-time worst transfer window READ MORE :

He told Sky Sports: "Obviously I'm confident as a player, so I don't think about the future and what the club will do in this position. I'm thinking how to improve and settle as fast as possible in the club because I have the opportunity to train directly with the team from the beginning of the season, to play the friendly games and then to go to official games.

"So it's a chance to play directly from the beginning - and then it's up to me to show the qualities and what I can bring in the team. I'm pretty confident that I will show it in the next games."

‌



Arsenal are not short of depth in the final third, but adding more firepower is one of their summer priorities. Tzolis will battle with the likes of Gabriel Martinelli, Noni Madueke and Eberechi Eze for a starting role - and the Gunners could yet add Vinicius before the summer is over.

View 2 Images Arsenal's new signing Christos Tzolis is determined to nail down a regular spot

Their interest in the Real Madrid star is well documented and they want to seize on the uncertainty surrounding his future with contract talks rumbling on in Spain.

‌



Vinicius returned to the club for his first pre-season training session on Monday following his World Cup campaign with Brazil. Jose Mourinho wants the winger to remain at Real but his wage demands are proving a sticking point.

Los Blancos do not want to lose him for nothing, which would be the case next summer when his contract expires. But the major stumbling block in negotiations is Vinicius' want to be the team's top earner, ahead of Kylian Mbappe. Real want to maintain their salary structure and the Frenchman currently sits top of their wage list.

Sports.title: Managing Newcastle as new striker added and Bruno Guimaraes makes final call
Sports.content:
Managing Newcastle as new striker added and Bruno Guimaraes makes final call

Newcastle United's incoming manager Matthias Jaissle has a lot of big decisions to make in his first transfer window at the helm

View 3 Images Matthias Jaissle will have plenty on his plate at Newcastle (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

It has been a challenging summer for Newcastle United but fans will hope the appointment of new manager Matthias Jaissle leads to some more positive transfer news. Al-Ahli boss Jaissle looks poised to take over following the departure of Eddie Howe and he will have work to do.

‌



Things have moved more quickly than at this stage of last summer's window, when Anthony Elanga was the only player to arrive before the start of August. More than £130million has been spent on new signings, though there have also been high-profile exits.

‌



Ivorian winger Bazoumana Toure has joined, ostensibly as a replacement for Anthony Gordon after the England star joined Barcelona. Sandro Tonali has also left, joining Tottenham in a deal worth up to £100m, with young midfielders Sean Steur and Aladji Bamba moving to St James' Park in an effort to soften the blow.

‌



In goal, new arrivals Ewen Jaouen and Lukas Hornicek have both joined. This is expected to pave the way for Nick Pope to leave the club, while experienced heads including Kieran Trippier and Emil Krafth have already moved on.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Arsenal target Bruno Guimaraes complies with Newcastle requests as midfielder touches down READ MORE :

There are still a number of matters which need to be resolved, though, not least the future of captain Bruno Guimaraes. Here, we've taken a look at what Jaissle can do to set the Magpies on the right path for the new campaign.

‌



Add midfield experience

While Bruno Guimaraes remains at Newcastle for now and a bid has been rejected, he is expected to be an Arsenal player by the end of the window. Ideally, they will want to avoid a repeat of last year when the Alexander Isak transfer saga dragged out to the point that they arguably overpaid on both Nick Woltemade and Yoane Wissa.

Tonali has already gone and Joelinton could yet follow amid reports of Saudi Pro League interest. Bamba and Steur have arrived with high ceilings but trusting your midfield operations to two players under the age of 21 feels like a risk Newcastle can't afford to take.

View 3 Images Newcastle have knocked back a bid for Bruno Guimaraes (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



If two more midfielders end up joining, Croatian World Cup star Petar Sucic could end up being one of them. Reports in Italy suggest the Inter Milan talent could be available for just over £38m, though Leeds are also keen.

Another man linked with a move is former Nottingham Forest man Danilo. Sporting director Ross Wilson brought the Brazil international to England back in 2023 and now could repeat the trick in the north east, with ESPN reporting in July that he is considered a potential replacement should Guimaraes depart.

Convince Lewis Hall to stay

Newcastle might well end up fighting a losing battle on their skipper, which makes it all the more important that they come out on the right side as far as Hall is concerned. The left-back has been a revelation since joining from Chelsea but that has naturally brought interest.

‌



Manchester United's interest appears to be the most concrete, with reports of a £60m opening bid in the near future. Michael Carrick's side are said to have internally approved a move for a player who they consider a long-term successor to Luke Shaw.

View 3 Images Lewis Hall has been involved for Newcastle in pre-season (Image: MI News/NurPhoto/Shutterstock)

Hall is under contract until 2029, though, so incoming boss Jaissle ought not to be under huge pressure to sell. Keeping the defender on board would send a key message going into a first season with a new man in the dugout.

‌



Replace Alexander Isak's goals

It goes without saying that goals were a problem for Newcastle in Howe's final season at the helm. Isak scored 23 in the league in his final season for the club before completing a deadline day move to Liverpool and Woltemade, Wissa and Will Osula - the three nominal strikers tasked with replacing that tally - managed just 16 between them.

Wissa was the biggest disappointment, netting just once in the league as he endured an injury-hit season following a £50m move from Brentford. The arrival of Jaissle could offer him a fresh start, though, after he showed some sharpness with a return of three goals for DR Congo at the World Cup.

It may well still be the case that a new marquee striker signing is needed, putting the Tonali and Gordon money to good use. Out-of-favour Chelsea striker Liam Delap has been linked, while Jaissle's arrival could well increase noise over a potential St James' Park return for Ivan Toney, who thrived under the German at Al-Ahli last season and earned a World Cup call-up as a result.

Article continues below

“Never say never,” Toney told Sky Sports News in February when asked about a Premier League return. “I have goals I want to achieve here first, the club have signed me for a long period of time. I want to repay them and bring trophies. In football and life, you never know what’s around the corner. Who knows what the next step is?

Sports.title: Stokes confirms England coach ambitions, reveals McCullum exit 'surprise'
Sports.content:
Ben Stokes has said he would "absolutely" love to coach England one day, as he also suggested Brendon McCullum would still be in charge of the Test team had he not announced his own international retirement weeks beforehand.

Stokes gave up the England Test captaincy and retired from international cricket following his side's 2-1 series defeat to New Zealand in June, which followed a 4-1 Ashes loss to Australia over the winter.

Speaking at length for the first time since his retirement on the For The Love of Cricket podcast hosted by former team-mates Stuart Broad and Jos Buttler, the 35-year-old Stokes suggested he had 'definitely' retired for good and opened up on his longer-term goals.

"I want to be a coach," said Stokes.

"I know what I want to do in terms of staying within the game - which is to be a coach.

"Would I love to be coach of England one day? Absolutely. I would love to be able to do that. Do I think it's going to happen? I don't know. No idea.

"Then, further on from that, I don't know. I just really like the idea of being, again, in some form of leadership away from playing."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Stokes hit a match-winning century in his first game back for Durham after announcing his retirement from international duty

Stokes held the Test captaincy for four years from 2022, working alongside head coach McCullum as the pair reshaped England's playing style.

McCullum's exit from his Test role was announced two weeks after Stokes called time on his international playing career during the fourth day of England's third Test against New Zealand at Trent Bridge.

"I was [surprised]," said Stokes.

"If I hadn't made the decision that I made four weeks ago, Baz would still be coach.

"So it's my fault!"

On the discussions held between them around their respective exits, Stokes added: "When I told Baz [about Stokes' retirement] he was making toast and I just went 'oh, I'm done'. I'd obviously had discussions with him anyway and then told him over toast.

"Then, again, he was like 'yeah, I've been given the tap on the shoulder' and I was like 'oh'. But he's still very excited and very happy to be moving forward with the white-ball because he's doing a very good job there."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking to Michael Atherton on the Sky Sports Cricket Podcast, former Australian white-ball captain Aaron Finch labelled England cricket 'a circus' and admitted he's finding their current crisis amusing

Stokes on his 'concern' for Root over captaincy return and Brook snub

Stokes also had his say on the new era for the Test team after former New Zealand captain Stephen Fleming was confirmed as the side's new head coach and Joe Root reappointed captain.

Stokes said he spoke with Root, his long-time team-mate and predecessor as captain in 2017-2022, when the news broke and backed him to succeed in his second spell in the role. However, Stokes said he did have "concern" for his friend given how the role hung heavily on England's highest run-scorer last time.

"I love Rooty. I wish him nothing but success," said Stokes.

"I hope he goes on to achieve amazing things in his role of captain, and I think he's going to really enjoy it with Flem. He's a great man. I've worked with Flem before.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Joe Root gives his first interview since being reappointed England Test captain

"But I told Joe: 'my only worry is you'. And that's all I really care about now with Rooty just because I saw what he went through and how much he put himself through.

"He just always put the team first; he always came second. That is just my only concern with it: knowing what he went through last time he was in charge of the team because I don't want to see that ever happen again because I care for Joe a lot.

"But I wish him all the success in the world. I'm sure he's going to do great so I'm looking forward to seeing what the team does going forward."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Harry Brook pays tribute to Ben Stokes following his retirement from international cricket and insists that he is up to the challenge of becoming the next England Test captain

But Stokes did question why Harry Brook, the vice-captain of the Test team and the white-ball captain, had not been named as his replacement.

Rob Key, England men's managing director, said recently "I don't feel like this is the right time" for Brook to be named Test captain but that the 27-year-old's "time will come".

But Stokes argued: "If you think someone is going to be a good captain or a good leader, just give it to them.

"Brooky [was] made vice-captain. I'm not there anymore but even when I missed that Test match [against New Zealand] I was like 'why is Brooky not captain? He's vice-captain.'

"And I understood the reasoning why they were saying it, but I was still like, what message is that sending to him? He's vice-captain and the captain is not playing but he's not captain. Then the same again here.

"I had no leadership or captaincy experience when I took over. It was just thought I was going to be a good captain."

Stokes rules out 2027 Ashes return

The 35-year-old also appeared to firmly rule out any playing return in next summer's home Ashes series against Australia after Key said he "wouldn't be surprised" if the all-rounder came out of retirement.

"I never once thought, 'I'm just going to give it up and just keep going as a player'," said Stokes of his decision to retire as captain and player.

"I'm 35. If I'm not going to be captain, I think I'd find it tough to do it. Not saying because I'd find it tough to be led by someone else. I just think because I've given so much of this part of my career to my job, if I'm going to be play for England it's going to be as captain.

"I was very comfortable retiring from playing and not thinking about playing for England."

And asked squarely if he had "definitely" retired, Stokes replied: "Defo."

Sports.title: 'Hull must step up and lead Team Europe at Solheim Cup'
Sports.content:
Dame Laura Davies has called upon Charley Hull to "step up and lead" Team Europe at the Solheim Cup in September.

European skipper Anna Nordqvist named her four captain's picks on Monday to complete the home side's 12-player lineup that will try to win back the trophy from the USA from September 11-13 in the Netherlands.

Hull and Spain's Carlota Ciganda have the most Solheim Cup experience among the European squad, with both set to play at the event for an eighth time.

England's Hull has enjoyed a strong 2026, finishing in the top 10 at three of the five majors, most recently claiming a share of sixth at the AIG Women's Open over the weekend.

Davies, Europe's record holder for the most appearances at the Solheim Cup, told the Sky Sports Golf Podcast: "It's a really strong looking team. You've got the experience, some of them are young but really well experienced in Solheim Cup golf. I think it's a lovely blend.

"I think Charley will be the leader again and we'll need her to perform like she did before. I know it was in a losing performance over there in Virginia, but she's got to step up and lead that team out."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ireland's Leona Maguire, Spain's Julia Lopez Ramirez, France's Nastasia Nadaud and England's Mimi Rhodes have been named as Anna Nordqvist's Solheim Cup captain's picks for Team Europe.

Europe are without the experience of Georgia Hall and Madelene Sagstrom, with the former having given birth earlier this year and the latter due to do so in September.

And while Nordqvist leads as captain, the event will end a run of nine successive Solheim Cup playing appearances for the Swede.

Davies added: "We've lost a few of the stalwarts, obviously Georgia Hall with the baby and Sagstrom, another big loss. The captain obviously not playing.

"But what we have got is a good nucleus of players that have played a lot of Solheim Cups and then the younger players that are just keen as mustard and want to get out there and play."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Dame Laura Davies believes Charley Hull and Lottie Woad may feel like they missed an opportunity to win the AIG Women's Open at Royal Lytham & St Annes.

Nordqvist, who also appeared on the Sky Sports Golf Podcast after finalising her squad, is also expecting Hull to play a key role for the home team.

"You're just going to let Charley be Charley," Nordqvist said.

"It was really nice to see how much she really enjoyed the Solheim Cup last time in Washington. I know we lost, but just seeing her enjoy the whole experience, light up the team room just with her personality.

"It's great to see her playing probably the best golf of her life, being up there in majors. She lives for those moments, so I can't wait to see her tee it up."

'I wouldn't want to play against Maguire'

Among Nordqvist's four captain's picks was Ireland's Leona Maguire, who top scored as an unbeaten rookie in Europe's away win over Team USA in 2021 before making further appearances in 2023 and 2024.

The 31-year-old was the highest-ranked European player in the Rolex Women's World Golf Rankings not to qualify automatically, having posted three top-10 finishes on the LPGA Tour this season but missed the cut in four of the five majors.

Maguire was the only player with past Solheim Cup experience named among Nordqvist's picks, announced live on Sky Sports, with Spain's Julia Lopez Ramirez, France's Nastasia Nadaud and England's Mimi Rhodes the other selections.

Nordqvist said: "Leona just has that little special thing that you need in the Solheim Cup. I wouldn't want to play against her. I'm glad she's on my team.

Image: Team Europe's confirmed 12-player line-up for this year's Solheim Cup

"Her having such a good start in her first Solheim Cup in Inverness, we started calling her MVP because I think she had the most points or she played the most matches.

"But she's just fearless and she's kind of like just suited for that game. She has the mentality and the toughness of just bringing out the best when she needs it."

Davies insisted that Maguire was "an absolute lock" as a captain's pick, pointing to her strong record in the competition.

"She hasn't (had the best season), I think she'd freely admit that," Davies said. "But what she has got is eight and a half points out of 12 Solheim Cup matches played.

"That's all you need to see there. That's batting at around just under 70 per cent. That's an unbelievable Solheim Cup record.

"And let's not forget, in Virginia, she didn't get many points at all. So, before that, she was batting at probably 85, 90 per cent winning percentage.

"She was an absolute lock, no question about it."

Sports.title: UFC fighter Nascimento dies aged 34

Sports.title: Perfect Nation and Avionics face off in Ffos Las feature
Sports.content:
Tuesday's action comes from Ffos Las and Lingfield, with seven races from each live on Sky Sports Racing.

3.00 Ffos Las - Perfect Nation and Avionics feature

Promising two-year-olds Perfect Nation and Avionics headline a seven-runner field in the EBF Novice Stakes.

Perfect Nation, who dons the colours of the Basher Watts Syndicate, ran with plenty of promise behind top prospect Flann Sunna on debut. He took a step forward when winning in great fashion at Lingfield last time out, and the only disadvantage for him is shouldering a seven-pound penalty for that success.

Andrew Balding puts up Qatari jockey Ebrahim Nader aboard Avionics. The 150,000gns breeze-up purchase shaped nicely when going down three lengths to Vintage Stakes runner Undiscovered and should provide stiff opposition to Perfect Nation with the seven-pound weight advantage.

Of the rest, newcomer George Cross has the potential to challenge, with his dam out of Group Three winner and So Mi Dar, who also placed in the Prix de l'Opera. The title-chasing Oisin Murphy rides Midgham Man, who was slow into stride on debut but could pose more of a threat today.

4.30 Ffos Las - Well-bred Flagbearer debuts for Haggas

William Haggas places 485,000gns yearling Flagbearer in the Dandara Homes Maiden Stakes.

The Wathnan-owned Sea The Stars colt makes his three-year-old debut and is bred to be quite smart, given his dam is half-sister to Canadian Grade 1 winner Cannock Chase and multiple Group 1 winner Star Catcher. Both of those horses won impressively on their first starts at three.

The Roger Varian-trained Wootz also boasts a smart pedigree. His dam was listed-placed and is a sister to Grade 3 winner and Grade 1-placed Luck. He is also half-brother to useful French three-year-old winner Marchon. The pedigree of both aforementioned horses suggests middle-distance trips will very much be their forte in due course.

Current jockeys' championship leader Billy Loughnane partners Arbaawy, who sets a relatively high standard on form. Although well-beaten in a competitive handicap at Ascot last time out, that race has produced some high-profile winners, including two at the recent Glorious Goodwood festival. Don't be surprised if he gets back to winning ways.

Vincenzo Bellini hung left in the straight on debut after being slow away and could come on for that run under Callum Hutchinson. Returning to tackle the same course and distance, Mark Loughnane's gelding will be partnered with Callum Hutchinson.

7.18 Lingfield - In-form duo Taritino and Tabasko clash

The in-form duo, Taritino and Tabasko lock horns in the Trusted Betting Site Comparison gambling.com Handicap.

Taritino is very much exposed now at the age of six, yet he has been in fine form - winning twice and placing twice in four starts since returning from hurdling. He remains fairly handicapped, and with the 14 furlongs likely to suit, a bold showing must be on the cards.

The progressive three-year-old Tabasko has been incredibly consistent this season, only going down narrowly at Doncaster last month. He can continue to improve and use his three-year-old weight allowance to his advantage against these older horses, with Ashley Lewis taking a further three pounds off.

With the emphasis likely to be on speed in just a four-runner field, Russian Rumour will probably not be seen to great effect, as Scarlet Moon would become a serious threat if a three-month break can see him bounce back to form. He returns to the Flat today after a solid stint over hurdles.

Sports.title: Itauma receives surprise IBF world title shot against Hrgovic
Sports.content:
Moses Itauma will fight for the vacant IBF world heavyweight title when he faces Filip Hrgovic in London on August 29.

Oleksandr Usyk announced his decision to vacate the WBC, WBA and IBF belts last month and the unbeaten British contender now has the opportunity to become the new IBF world champion in his clash with Croatian Hrgovic at The O2.

Frank Sanchez, who is the IBF No 1 contender after his knockout victory over Richard Torrez Jnr in May, has been guaranteed a shot at the Itauma vs Hrgovic winner.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Moses Itauma and Filip Hrgovic were both in a confident mood ahead of their heavyweight showdown in August.

Itauma has blazed his path to a world title shot with 14 victories, featuring 12 knockouts, and he ruthlessly stopped Jermaine Franklin in Manchester in March.

But the 21-year-old is taking a sizeable step up in class against Hrgovic, who holds victories over Zhilei Zhang and Joe Joyce, with his only loss coming against Daniel Dubois by stoppage in 2024.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Moses Itauma delivers 'beautiful' knockout to stop Jermaine Franklin in the fifth-round of their bout at Manchester's Co-op Live Arena. Pictures courtesy of X @DAZN.

Cuban Sanchez will lie in wait for the new IBF champion, having secured a mandatory shot at the IBF belt after his explosive second-round stoppage of Torrez Jr.

The IBF belt is the last remaining vacant title as Agit Kabayel has been elevated as the new WBC champion, while Murat Gassiev has been upgraded to WBA champion.

Sports.title: F1 2027 calendar contingency plans in place amid Middle East conflict
Sports.content:
Formula 1 president Stefano Domenicali has confirmed contingency plans are in place for the 2027 F1 calendar if the conflict in the Middle East continues next year.

In recent seasons, F1 has previously revealed its calendar for the following year by now but will not announce the 2027 schedule until the autumn.

Domenicali says a "normal plan" will be announced but is aware of the ongoing US-Israel war with Iran which already cancelled this year's Bahrain and Saudi Arabian Grands Prix, and the current season will end in Europe should the Qatar and Abu Dhabi Grands Prix not take place.

"In case the situation in the Middle East is not solved, we have options, different plans [for 2027]. But the trigger for that, of course, is at the end of the year, so we have still a lot of time to adjust," said Domenicali.

"But if the situation in that region is not solved for next year, F1 is a marginal point on which we should be worried marginally because the situation will be very bad.

"Just to assure you, we have different plans with different options already in place that will accommodate the fact that we will keep, in any case, the target of 24 races also for next year."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Formula 1 has added Malaysia to its 2026 schedule to host the Bahrain Grand Prix that was postponed earlier in the season

F1 in talks with countries for new races

F1 has already announced Turkey and Portugal will return to the calendar to replace Zandvoort, which will host the final Dutch Grand Prix on August 21-23 after the summer break, and Barcelona.

Any new events would only join the 2028 calendar, at the earliest, but F1 are in talks with Rwanda, South Africa, Thailand and Argentina - the latter primarily due to the sport's surge in popularity since Franco Colapinto joined the grid.

"Negotiations are progressing very well in Africa. We are having other discussions in South America. We have discussions in the Far East," said Domenicali.

"One thing that I can tell you is that we have more requests in China and Japan, but for the moment, we want to stay with one race in China because we need to consolidate the market before thinking about having other options there."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the best bits of the chaotic Lego parade at the British Grand Prix

Germany has also emerged as a surprise contender to join future calendars with the possibility of Hockenheim returning to the schedule.

F1 last raced at Hockenheim in 2019 but a lack of government investment saw the track fall off the calendar. However, the venue now has a different ownership and investment model.

"It was Hockenheim that connected with us, and they had the first discussion," said Domenicali.

"They are developing the motorsport park there with a different objective. If they want to discuss a possible F1 event, of course the investment needs to be different - because our platform needs to have a different kind of investment. But we have discussed that."

He added: "We are watching the growth in Europe because it's becoming an important market again because the numbers are there."

Sports.title: Short guides Welsh Fire to crucial win over Southern Brave
Sports.content:
A superb unbeaten half-century from Matt Short guided Welsh Fire to a six-wicket victory over Southern Brave that takes them level on points at the top The Hundred table.

With both sides still in the hunt for a qualification place and coming off the back of morale-boosting victories, it was the Fire who took the honours in Cardiff to join Trent Rockets on 16 points at the summit of the table.

Opting to bowl, Fire's battery of experienced seamers were immediately into the action, Chris Woakes and Sam Cook reducing the Brave to 2-2 off seven balls as Jamie Smith and Ben McKinney both edged behind to Phil Salt.

The Cook-Salt combo also accounted for Nikhil Chaudhary after he and Marcus Stoinis had sedately taken the visitors to an underwhelming 45-3 at the halfway stage.

Not long after, Rachin Ravindra, getting big turn, snared Tristan Stubbs and Moeen Ali with successive deliveries, the latter caught by Joe Root off a skier.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Moeen Ali goes for a golden duck, leaving the Southern Brave in trouble against the Welsh Fire

The Brave were chugging along at barely a run a ball on a tricky surface but Stoinis added some muscular impetus, going to a 35-ball half-century before hitting Cook, who returned a magnificent 3-14, down deep square's throat.

David Miller hit a couple of late sixes but Short, coming on to bowl for the first time in the final five of the innings, had him caught on the edge.

Jofra Archer hit a first-ball six but was gone second ball and the Brave ended with 115-8, their lowest-ever total in The Hundred, below their 118-8 against the Oval Invincibles in 2024.

With little margin for error, Archer set the tone for the Fire, delighting in getting Phil Salt with his first ball and not conceding a run until his eighth.

But Short and Root kept things moving, knowing that one or two partnerships would be enough, and calmly took the score to 60 off 48 before Root departed, caught by McKinney off Chris Jordan.

Ravindra and Jordan Cox came and went but Tom Kohler-Cadmore kept the scoreboard ticking over as he supported Short - who reached a 37-ball 50 with a scoop off Archer and made good use of the ramp throughout to the short straight boundaries - to see his side home, an anticlimactic two wides finishing things.

Image: Matt Short (left) and Tom Kohler-Cadmore saw Welsh Fire to victory over the Southern Brave

Match Hero Matt Short said: "It was tough early and it was a pretty spicy wicket with some quick bowlers. It was nice to bat second and get a bit of dew and skid off the wicket.

"They came hard with a Test match length but the shine wears off and it gets a bit easier. When we bowled, our guys hit the right length and let the ball do the talking."

Despite having won four of their five games, the Fire have a negative net run rate of -0.081, while leaders Trent Rockets are on +0.760.

The Brave, who have now played more matches than any other side in the men's tournament, fell to a fourth defeat in six and are facing a battle to advance.

What's next in The Hundred?

The Hundred continues on Tuesday with SunRisers Leeds hosting London Spirit at Headingley. The women's fixture begins at 3pm, with the men's contest following at 6.30pm.
