Sports.title: ‘Doesn’t make sense’ – West Ham warned they’re making transfer ‘mistake’
Sports.content:
West Ham are making a 'mistake' by selling Freddie Potts, according to former Hammers star Kevin Nolan.

talkSPORT understands that Potts has been granted permission to travel to Belgium to undergo a medical ahead of a £10million move to Belgian side Club Brugge.

2 Potts, who has been with West Ham since he was six, is on the cusp of a £10m move to Belgian side Club Brugge Credit: Getty

The midfielder was expected to play a key role for West Ham in the coming Championship campaign as the Hammers seek an immediate Premier League return.

And yet, Potts is now set to leave the London Stadium, ending a 17-year association with the east London outfit.

Nolan, who spent four years on the West Ham books, revealed to Alex Crook on talkSPORT on Monday that he is 'surprised' that the capital side are cashing in on the 22-year-old.

"I think this probably could turn out to be a bit of a mistake, but it's good money for Freddie," Nolan said.

"I think it's a great move for Freddie to go to Club Brugge and be able to play in Europe, and play the style he wants.

"I'm quite surprised that this has been allowed to happen, if I'm honest.

"I thought that he could be one of the players who could stand up this year for West Ham.

"It doesn't make sense to me, but I wish Freddie all the luck because he's a great kid, lovely family, and I'm sure he'll go and be successful over there."

2 Potts' impending exit has caught a number of club legends off guard Credit: Getty

'I don't get it'

Nolan's comments on Potts echo Tony Cottee's words on the player's impending exit.

Former Hammers striker Cottee joined Jeff Stelling and Andy Townsend on talkSPORT Breakfast where he admitted his disappointment at seeing the 22-year-old go.

"I don't get it. Freddie Potts, I don't know I might be a bit biased," he said.

"I played with his dad and I want to see the academy players. I don't get it, £10million to Brugge, I think they're talking about.

"When he played in the Championship two seasons ago, he was Player of the Year for Portsmouth, he was the Player of the Year for Wycombe in League One and we're getting rid of a good young academy player.

"It doesn't make sense to me at all. Alright, £10million, you could argue that the club needs a bit of money to pay the bills.

"I get that at the moment, but in the grand scale of things, you've got to keep your good academy boys.

"West Ham might have raised well over £200million by the time the season starts.

"At which point, why are you selling an academy player for £10million? I don't get that one."

Sports.title: Inside the latest on Jack Grealish’s future as ‘fake reports’ dismissed
Sports.content:
Gabby Agbonlahor has hit out at 'fake reports' surrounding the reason Jack Grealish missed Manchester City's pre-season tour of Asia.

Grealish was a notable omission from the travelling squad, with rumours circulating he was left in England deliberately.

2 Grealish hasn't played since suffering a foot injury on loan at Everton Credit: instagram @jackgrealish

The City forward corrected one outlet's report that he and teammate Kalvin Phillips had been 'left out of' the selection that flew to the Far East.

"Just to let you know I’m still recovering from an injury so I’m not training yet. Haven’t been left out so stop talking poo poo thanks," Grealish wrote on an Instagram post.

And Agbonlahor has reinforced Grealish's claims as the pair discussed the latter's future while on holiday.

When asked about the possibility of returning to Aston Villa on Drive on Monday, Agbonlahor said: "I don't think so."

The talkSPORT pundit then elaborated: "I didn't have a conversation about Villa, I had a conversation about his future.

"There's been so many fake reports about how he wasn't called for the (pre-season) tour and he wasn't wanted, that's all nonsense.

"He's not able to train yet, so he's been out training at Real Mallorca's training ground, been putting the hard yards in, looking after himself, training hard.

"He just said he's hungry. If it's at Manchester City, if it's another club - I can't say which one it is - he wants to play football, he wants to get back."

The Greal Deal

Grealish spent last season on loan with Merseyside outfit Everton, and made a bright start to life at Hill Dickinson Stadium.

Indeed, the 30-year-old managed two goals and six assists but his time under David Moyes was cut short due to a foot injury sustained against former side Villa back in January.

2 Grealish started brightly at Everton before a foot injury cut his time on Merseyside short Credit: Getty

A potential return to Everton was discussed on Drive, to which Agbonlahor, who had previously defended Grealish, said: "It could be an option, why not?

"David Moyes loves him, he knows the club, and there's talk about (Iliman) Ndiaye going to Saudi Arabia.

"I think whatever happens, whatever club he joins, if it's at Man City or he goes back to Everton, or another club, he's hungry.

"He's in his last year as well - in your last year, you need to be playing football, you need to be performing."

"Look, for instance, at Jadon Sancho now, it's a shame to see (him without a club), he's 26, I don't know who he's training with."

Agbonlahor's comments come after new City head coach Enzo Maresca previously admitted he is yet to speak with Grealish.

"I didn't speak with Jack while I am here. Jack is a City player. When we are back in Manchester, if he is fit he will work with us," the Italian said.

Sports.title: Middlesbrough vs Wrexham LIVE commentary: Kick-off time, team news and where to watch Carabao Cup tie for free
Sports.content:
Middlesbrough vs Wrexham LIVE commentary: Kick-off time, team news and where to watch Carabao Cup tie for free

The English domestic football season is finally back - and first up, it's the Carabao Cup that takes centre stage.

In an unusual change, the first round of the competition is being held before the EFL kickstarts their new campaign.



3 The first round of the Carabao Cup kicks off this week Credit: Getty

And in one of the opening games, Championship rivals Middlesbrough and Wrexham clash at the Riverside Stadium.

Boro just missed out on a place in the Premier League last season, losing in the play-off final to Hull City after being handed a place in the showpiece due to Southampton's Spygate scandal.

Middlesbrough boss Kim Hellberg will want to come out fighting again this term, and he'll be keen to get things going with a cup win.



As for Wrexham, they finished one place outside the play-offs and reached the fourth round of the Carabao Cup last season.

Phil Parkinson's side will hope to go deeper into the competition this time around as they eye another Hollywood story.



Middlesbrough vs Wrexham: talkSPORT coverage

This Carabao Cup first round tie will take place on Friday, August 7, with kick-off at the Riverside set for 8pm.

talkSPORT will have live commentary of the game from Mark Wilson and former Newcastle defender Steve Howey.



Listen talkSPORT through the website or find us on DAB digital radio through your smart speaker and on 1089 or 1053 AM.

Download and listen to all our live commentaries via the talkSPORT app.

For the latest odds and bet boosts for every big event, visit talkSPORT BET.

Subscribe to the talkSPORT YouTube channel for news, views and analysis plus our regular goals show and for more, 



3 Wrexham reached the fourth round of the Carabao Cup last season Credit: Getty

The all-Championship clash will also be broadcast free-to-air on ITV, with the game also streamed online on ITVX.

Sky Sports will be broadcasting the action too.

Middlesbrough vs Wrexham: Team news

Middlesbrough will hope that star attacker Morgan Whittaker is available to feature amid interest from West Ham.

Meanwhile, new signings Sebastian Berhalter, Will Lankshear and Jeremy Sarmiento could all make their cup debuts.



Leo Castledine, a 21-year-old attacking midfielder, scored two in Boro's final friendly.

3 Whittaker is attracting interest from West Ham this summer Credit: Getty

In the Wrexham camp, Danny Imray could start his first competitive game for the club after making his debut in pre-season.

Kieffer Moore is likely to lead the line, with Sam Smith, Nathan Broadhead and Bailey Cadamarteri all available too.



Full-back Liberato Cacace missed a lot of football last term through injury, but he should be fit to now play regularly.

Middlesbrough vs Wrexham: Pre-season results

Middlesbrough drew their last pre-season game 3-3 against Espanyol, to end their preparations with a thriller.

They lost 3-1 to Huddersfield and drew 1-1 with Scottish champions Celtic in their other friendlies.

Wrexham spent their pre-season on a tour of the United States, playing three Premier League opponents.



They beat Leeds 3-2 in their first clash but were beaten 1-0 by Liverpool and then lost by the same scoreline to Sunderland.

However, Parkinson's men did win 1-0 against Manchester United in Finland before heading to the States.

Sports.title: Former Arsenal goalkeeper, 38, keeps clean sheet in Carabao Cup match - 18 months after his last competitive appearance
Sports.content:
Former Arsenal goalkeeper, 38, keeps clean sheet in Carabao Cup match - 18 months after his last competitive appearance

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Former Arsenal goalkeeper Vito Mannone enjoyed a positive debut for Crawley Town on Monday night, keeping a clean sheet as his new side knocked out York City in the preliminary round of the Carabao Cup.

Mannone, who was signed by Arsene Wenger in 2005 and would go on to make 15 appearances for the Gunners before his eventual departure in 2013, joined Crawley Town earlier this summer in a dual player-coach role.

The 38-year-old was solid between the sticks, making two saves as Gianmarco Di Biase and Danilo Orsi's goals ensured Crawley Town's season got off on the front foot at the LNER Community Stadium on Monday.

Some of the visiting fans serenaded former coach Scott Lindsey, who was axed by Crawley earlier in the year before taking the reins at newly promoted League Two side York last week, with chants of 'sacked in the morning' following Di Biase's 24th-minute opener.

Mannone, however, had a less controversial first game, bringing his extensive experience to the League Two outfit as they look to improve on a campaign which only narrowly avoided relegation on the final day last term.

Crawley are now set to visit Watford on Saturday in the Carabao Cup's first round. Their league season gets underway next weekend against Crewe.

Vito Mannone joined Crawley Town earlier this summer on a dual player-coach role

Mannone was signed by Arsene Wenger in 2005 and would go on to make 15 appearances for the Gunners before his eventual departure for Sunderland in 2013

It was Mannone's first competitive match in 18 months, having last turned out for Lille in February 2025 before leaving the French side as a free agent at the end of the season.

He had most recently been working at Premier League club Brighton as an Academy Goalkeeper Coach and was a UEFA A GK Candidate before joining Crawley in June.

Mannone will head up the goalkeeping department, taking control of all sessions and player development, but will also be available for selection as a registered member of the playing squad.

Crawley manager Colin Kazim-Richards told the club website: 'To be able to add to my coaching staff, to the club, someone of Vito's calibre is a credit in itself.

'His knowledge, his footballing experiences, playing at the highest level with some of the best coaches in terms of standards – what it actually takes and ideas coming from a country that creates amazing goalkeepers – has really taken us up another level.

'Vito comes with an intensity, and it's something I'm looking forward to in terms of creating a relationship and benefiting from his skills from a goalkeeper's perspective, and also as a person.

'As soon as we spoke, I knew he was the right man, so I can't wait to work with him.'

The 6ft 2in Italian has enjoyed a well-travelled career since joining Wenger in north London from Atalanta's academy at the age of 17.

After a loan spell at Barnsley in the 2006-07 season, Mannone became a regular around Arsenal's first team, working alongside Manuel Almunia and Lukasz Fabianski before making his debut against Stoke City in May 2009.

His stock rose during an eight-game stint for the Gunners in the 2009-10 campaign, although he lost his place when Almunia returned from injury. Two season-long spells with Hull City followed before he joined Sunderland in 2013.

The Italian's stock rose during an eight-game stint for the Gunners in the 2009-10 campaign, although he lost his place when Almunia returned from injury

Mannone would go on to make 80 appearances for Sunderland before moving to Reading in the summer of 2017.

Following a two-year stint with the Royals, and a period on loan with Major League Soccer side Minnesota United, where Mannone was named MLS Goalkeeper of the Year, the shot-stopper returned to the continent and enjoyed spells at Esbjerg FB, AS Monaco, FC Lorient and Lille before departing at the end of the 2025-26 season.

Following his appointment at Crawley, Mannone said: 'I am delighted and proud to take on this role and can’t wait to meet everyone at the club and to start working with the staff and players.

'I’ll give everything to the cause and hope to pass on my experiences as a player, leading into a successful season.'

Sports.title: Newlywed tennis power couple Katie Boulter and Alex de Minaur sign up for star-studded US Open mixed doubles - as Aryna Sabalenka partners Novak Djokovic and Jack Draper returns to partner billionaire talent Jessica Pegula
Sports.content:
Newlywed tennis power couple Katie Boulter and Alex de Minaur 

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Tennis power couple Katie Boulter and Alex de Minaur have joined the entry list for the US Open's star-studded mixed doubles one month on from their wedding in Tuscany.

The former British No1 and the world No5 married in Siena, before celebrating at the picturesque Borgo Santo Pietro luxury hotel, days after a small family ceremony in Boulter's home county of Leicestershire.

The couple are now set to try and play their first tournament as husband and wife, after previously showing off their skills in the format at Wimbledon three years ago.

The US Open launched their revamped mixed doubles tournament last year with the aim of bringing a new audience to the competition on the eve of the main draw singles matches.

Unlike traditional Grand Slam doubles draws, the United States Tennis Association (USTA) tempted big-name singles players to pair up, such as the much-discussed partnership of Carlos Alcaraz and Emma Raducanu.

De Minaur and Boulter entered last year, but just missed out on a place in the competition in a packed field.

Newly married couple Alex de Minaur and Katie Boulter have entered themselves for the US Open's mixed doubles

The Australian-British couple married last month in Siena at Borgo Santo Pietro luxury hotel

Those who take part in the two-day event can book their spot through direct entry, with six teams chosen based on the pair's combined singles ranking

There will then be eight additional pairs handed a wildcard for the main draw. This year, two further teams will be added after going through qualifying - for which six teams play by virtue of their ranking, with two more wildcards given out for this earlier stage.

The married couple joined the entry list in a second wave of entrants, with other boldfaced name partnerships announced last month.

Standout pairs all but guaranteed a spot in the main draw include world No1 Aryna Sabalenka and Novak Djokovic, Elena Rybakina and US men's No1 Taylor Fritz, and Iga Swiatek and Casper Ruud.

Boulter and De Minaur are also not the only couple to have entered, with new duo Elena-Gabriela Ruse and Nuno Borges announced in the first wave, and husband and wife team Elina Svitolina and Gael Monfils joining the cohort in the second.

Former British No1 Jack Draper has paired up for a second year in a row with Jessica Pegula, the US women's No1, with the unlikely duo reaching the semi-final.

Pegula shared this week that the pair had found each other again with a view to 'running it back', but Draper will face a nervous wait for a US Open main draw wildcard to allow him to play alongside Pegula rather than taking part in singles qualifying.

Boulter and De Minaur had previously enjoyed a small family ceremony in Leicestershire

Last year's breakout pair Jack Draper and Jessica Pegula are teaming up for a second year

But the much-discussed pairing of Emma Raducanu and Carlos Alcaraz won't be able to team up again as the former continues to recover from a stress fracture

New pairs announced alongside De Minaur and Boulter include Anna Kalinskaya and Lorenzo Musetti, Wimbledon finalist Karolina Muchova teaming up with fellow Czech Jakub Mensik, and tennis icon Venus Williams partnering Alexander Bublik.

New teams could yet be announced before the entry window closes on August 17, with a number of intriguing names - such as Jannik Sinner's, Carlos Alcaraz's and Serena Williams' - not yet paired up.

Raducanu will be unable to team up with Alcaraz for a second year in a row after news broke on Monday that the British No1 will not be able to compete in New York at all as she continues to recover from her grade four stress fracture.

Despite its eye-popping $1million prize, the new-look mixed doubles features a shortened format that allows for multiple matches to be played across the two night sessions.

Until the semi-finals, best-of-three matches will feature sets played to four, with no-advantage scoring and a 10-point tiebreak in lieu of a third set. From then on, matches are played to six games.

Sports.title: Alan Brazil announces return to radio after his heart stopped beating on the operating table during life-saving liver transplant
Sports.content:
Alan Brazil has revealed he will return to the radio on Wednesday just a few months after having a life-saving liver transplant.

The talkSPORT stalwart has been off-air for almost four months but will now return to present his regular Breakfast Show slot alongside former Premier League striker Gabby Agbonlahor.

Brazil, 67, shared in June that he had undergone life-saving surgery and disclosed that he was on the operating table for eight hours, admitting his heart had stopped before restarting itself.

Now ready to return to radio, Brazil cut a relaxed figure as he delivered a video update on social media on Monday.

'Hugo, say hello,' the Scot said while petting his dog in the video.

'I'm looking forward to Wednesday. Wednesday at 6am - talkSPORT, Brazil's back. Looking forward to it.

Alan Brazil has revealed in a video on social media that he will return to talkSPORT radio at 6am on Wednesday just a few months after having a liver transplant

Brazil, pictured holding a red wine next to Dean Saunders, described the surgery as life saving

'I've had a great break here in Suffolk, the weather's been sensational although I'm not allowed to be in the sun too much. But it's been great.

'The World Cup - not so great for me. I didn't like all the commercialisation and of course we're hearing all about it now, aren't we?'

At this point in the video, his dog Hugo then leaps off the sofa, prompting Brazil to say: 'There you go, I'm just about to talk about Gabby (Agbonlahor) and Hugo's p***ed off.

'Wednesday morning, it looks like Gabby and me just after six o'clock, all being well I'll be back on. I'm going to have Thursday off because I've got a couple of treatments I've got to do, and then Friday I'll be back at six as well.

'Hopefully it'll be Ray Parlour - Party Parlour - I spoke to him yesterday and he was enjoying himself as normal. Some Sunday lunch in Essex, some swanky restaurant having a great time.

In June, Brazil spoke about how his heart stopped on the operating table during surgery

The Scot, pictured after the surgery in June, is looking forward to getting back on the radio

'I've missed all this guys over the last three months, I really have. And I've had a great break. I feel my voice and everything is beginning to improve week after week. I'm still not there yet, nowhere near - it'll take another three, four, maybe six months but I'm definitely a lot better.

'I can't wait, I've taken some season tickets to Ipswich this year, so I'm going to spend a lot of time at Portman Road. Things are great.'

Brazil went on to deliver his thoughts ahead of the new Premier League season, branding Arsenal as the 'team to beat' and tipping Liverpool, Manchester United and Tottenham to have strong campaigns.

He also revealed that Ally McCoist, who regularly joins Brazil on talkSPORT, is enjoying a 'much-deserved' break after working as a pundit throughout the World Cup.

Brazil finished the video saying: 'Anyway, it's great to be back, I feel good. I'm looking forward to Wednesday morning, just after six o'clock with Gabby Agbonlahor on talkSPORT. We'll get it going again!'

Brazil has presented the Breakfast show since the radio station launched in 2000, cutting back his hours in 2020.

In March, he was forced to miss his presenting duties for talkSPORT during the final two days at Cheltenham Festival. Brazil previously had a spell off air in January due to illness too.

The former striker started his football career at Ipswich Town in 1976 and later had spells at Tottenham and Man United in the 1980s.

He won 13 caps for Scotland - representing them at the 1982 World Cup in Spain - but struggled with back issues towards the end of his career.

Sports.title: Revealed: The eye-watering £18.5m contract Real Madrid 'offer Vinicius Jr' amid Arsenal's interest in Brazilian superstar
Sports.content:
Revealed: The eye-watering £18.5m contract Real Madrid 'offer Vinicius Jr' amid Arsenal's interest in Brazilian superstar

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Real Madrid are believed to have offered Vinicius Junior a hefty salary increase which could see the Brazil star earn a staggering £18.5million (€22m) per year against the backdrop of keen interest in the player from Arsenal.

The Gunners made initial enquiries into the player last week, with manager Mikel Arteta insisting that the Premier League winners will be 'very ambitious' during the summer's transfer window.

But Daily Mail Sport reported on Monday that Los Blancos had responded in kind by re-opening transfer talks with Vinicius after earlier discussions had stalled last season.

According to ESPN, on the table is an increased salary which could give him a rise of almost £4m, with Vinicius' current deal believed to see him rake in £14.9m per season.

Vinicius is not thought to have an issue with the salary on offer from president Florentino Perez, however, the parties are yet to reach an agreement on a potential signing-on fee.

It is also not yet clear how long the new contract ties Vinicius to the club, with the player's current deal coming to an end in less than a year.

Real Madrid have offered Vinicius Junior an eye-watering salary increase as they attempt to pin him down with a new deal

The Brazilian striker returned to his club's set-up on Monday after his post-World Cup break

Should Vinicius not sign a new deal, Real Madrid would be forced to see one of their marquee players depart on a free transfer, with the possibility of him signing a pre-contract from January.

The player is thought to view any contract he signs with Los Blancos, where he has played since 2018, as the defining deal of his career - and recognition of his efforts for the club that in recent seasons have seen him become a Ballon d'Or contender in their colours.

Vinicius returned to join his team-mates at their pre-season camp on Monday to undergo the standard start-of-season medical tests and train for the first time under new manager Jose Mourinho.

Arteta meanwhile has remained bullish about his plans for the rest of the window, following the £34m signing of Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge.

‘We expect to have movements in the next few weeks, obviously,’ Arteta said following Arsenal's pre-season friendly against Girona.

‘We want to get better like anybody else, and you can see the transfer market and our opponents... We won't sit still and we are very ambitious with what we are doing.

‘The margins are very small. Because we want to get better and the level is going to increase.

'We need to increase the competition internally. We need to make sure we identify the things that we don't have in the team.’

But the Gunners have already been rebuffed in their pursuit of Bruno Guimaraes, with Newcastle turning down a bid from north London.

Sports.title: Who will win the 2026 Ballon d'Or? Bookies reveal clear favourite as Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe and Lionel Messi seek prestigious honour - but will one of Spain's World Cup heroes take the prize?
Sports.content:
Who will win the 2026 Ballon d'Or? Bookies reveal clear favourite as Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe and Lionel Messi seek prestigious honour - but will one of Spain's World Cup heroes take the prize?

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

With the World Cup having concluded, Harry Kane, Lionel Messi and Lamine Yamal will be among the stars with their sights set on football's ultimate personal accolade, the Ballon d’Or.

Performances of several stars at the tournament have furthered their claims for the honour, with several Spain stars surging up the list of favourites after playing key roles in their triumph.

The Ballon d'Or will officially be announced on October 26.

Will there be a repeat winner or will a new name be on the honour roll for the third consecutive year?

Daily Mail Sport takes a look at the possible contenders to receive the prestigious prize.

Ousmane Dembele won last year's Ballon d'Or and is among the contenders again for the award

Harry Kane – Evens

Heading up this list of possible winners is England captain and Bayern Munich’s No9, Harry Kane.

Kane has been at the peak of the footballing world for over a decade now, but has a serious chance of becoming the first Englishman since Michael Owen in 2001 to win the Ballon d'Or after the best statistical season of his career.

The 33-year-old scored a staggering 61 goals in 51 matches last season for Bayern Munich to help the German giants achieve a domestic double, as well as reaching a Champions League semi-final.

Despite Bayern falling to PSG in the last four, Kane scored in both legs of the semi-final, as he had also done against Real Madrid in the previous round.

Kane was equally brilliant for England in the World Cup, having been instrumental as Thomas Tuchel's side progressed to the semi-finals.

The England captain scored six goals, including two braces, but his lack of involvement in their semi-final loss to Argentina could count against him.

Historically just two domestic trophies would not be enough to win the Ballon d’Or but Kane’s mind-boggling output over the past year means he remains the bookies' favourite to win the prestigious prize.

Harry Kane could become the first English player to win the Ballon d'Or since Michael Owen

Lamine Yamal – 9/4

Kane will have his work cut out for him though, as the second on the list of favourites for this year’s award is Lamine Yamal.

The Barcelona and Spain star is seen as having a strong chance to become the first teenager to win the Ballon d’Or.

Since the start of last season, Yamal has been simply unstoppable. The Spaniard enjoyed a stellar season for both club and country, winning La Liga, the Spanish Super Cup and of course the World Cup.

Yamal racked up an impressive 16 goals and 12 assists in 28 La Liga games, while he also netted six times and assisted four goals in the Champions League.

His contribution would have likely been even higher had Yamal not seen the end of his season blighted by injury. He made a speedy recovery in time for the World Cup and while he may have not been at his blistering best, the winger played a vital role.

The 19-year-old, who started all but one game, was crucial to Spain’s success, despite only scoring one goal.

The threat he posed forced teams to double up on him, providing open space for teammates. Yamal was also expert in drawing free kicks and penalties through his trickery. Even with a low output his effect was still felt.

Spain's World Cup success has boosted Lamine Yamal's chances following on from his stunning season with Barcelona

Rodri – 9/2

Spain's World Cup winning captain Rodri has emerged as a leading contender following the tournament.

Rodri is an interesting case amongst this year’s favourites and presents the voters with a dilemma.

To many captaining your side to a World Cup with eight flawless performances should immediately make you a top candidate for the honour, but Rodri’s year has been disrupted by several injuries, preventing him from playing half of the Premier League season.

When on the pitch Rodri has been outstanding and he was deservedly named as the World Cup's Player of The Tournament after orchestrating sublime victories over France and Argentina in the semi-final and final respectively.

Victory for Rodri would indicate that performances in the biggest games are key, rather than consistency over the course of 12 months.

Rodri's starring role for Spain at the World Cup has pushed him into contention for the honour

The Spain captain was named as the World Cup's best player after their final triumph

Kylian Mbappe – 6/1

While French superstar Mbappe went another season without a trophy, his individual performances and numbers have been typically magnificent over the past nine months.

With Real Madrid, Mbappe netted an impressive 42 goals in 44 games, including 15 in 11 Champions League outings to end as the top scorer in the competition.

Mbappe was undoubtedly one of the leading figures at the World Cup, scoring ten goals to win the golden boot, finishing clear of his nearest challenger Lionel Messi.

The haul also saw Mbappe become the outright leading goalscorer in World Cup history.

Despite Mbappe reiterating his individual brilliance once again, a lack of silverware may hold him back from winning his first Ballon d’Or.

Kylian Mbappe secured the golden boot at the World Cup, but a lack of silverware my hold him back

Lionel Messi – 8/1

The timeless talent of Messi never seems to fade.

Messi, viewed by many as the greatest of all time, showed us this summer that he is far from finished and remains decisive on the world stage.

Despite Argentina losing the final, Messi's World Cup performances alone could bring him an extraordinary ninth Ballon d’Or.

Messi silenced doubters from the first match, in which he scored a hat-trick against Algeria. He would go on to contribute goals and assists in all but one of Argentina’s World Cup matches, racking up eight and four respectively.

While it may not hold as much weight as European domestic success, in late 2025 Messi spearheaded Inter Miami to their first ever MLS Cup victory, scoring six goals and getting seven assists in just six MLS play-off games.

Despite his advancing years, Messi was the inspiration behind Argentina's path to the World Cup final

Ousmane Dembele – 12/1

Reigning Ballon d'Or winner Ousmane Dembele is in contention for back-to-back triumphs.

After years of ridicule and derision in the early 2020s, Dembele has been transformed from an underachieving talent to the world’s best under Luis Enrique at PSG.

For the second year running, Dembele won the Champions League with the French side. The forward held his nerve to score their all-important equaliser from the penalty spot in the final against Arsenal – his 20th goal of the season.

Dembele also enjoyed a prolific World Cup with the Frenchman scoring six goals, including an excellent hat-trick against Norway. But his lack of influence in helping Les Bleus past Spain in their semi-final may count against him.

Ousmane Dembele helped PSG retain the Champions League, putting him in contention for back-to-back Ballon d'Or triumphs

Jude Bellingham – 14/1

Bellingham’s reputation was already stellar before this year, but he became England's Birmingham Baggio as he attempted to drive the Three Lions to the World Cup final, akin to how the ponytailed star had done for Italy in the 1994 tournament.

Similarly to his Madrid teammate Kylian Mbappe, Bellingham failed to pick up any silverware and will be massively held back by that in the voting. However, it would be ignorant to not at least consider Bellingham for the prize.

The midfielder certainly possesses the talent to deserve the prestigious award. However, the award rarely goes to the most gifted footballer at the time, but rather the most successful in that year’s campaign.

So unfortunately for Bellingham, despite his heroic England performances and unquestionable quality, a season in which you win no silverware and register 13 goals and assists in 40 games is unlikely to cut it.

Jude Bellingham starred for England at the World Cup to put him in contention for the award

Pau Cubarsi and Fabian Ruiz – 16/1 and 18/1

Two Spain stars from their World Cup triumph are viewed as outsiders for the prize.

Teenager defender Cubarsi was named as the Best Young Player at the World Cup, with Spain having conceded just one goal on their route to winning the tournament.

Cubarsi is joined by midfielder Fabian Ruiz, who has won both the World Cup and Champions League this year.

Despite getting fewer than ten goals and assists across the club season and the World Cup, Ruiz's contribution to his club and country’s success through his ability to keep and advance possession amongst other abilities has been invaluable.

Pau Cubarsi was named as the best young player at the World Cup after starring in defence for Spain

Fabian Ruiz won both the World Cup with Spain and the Champions League with PSG

Luis de la Fuente's decision to start him over Pedri in the latter stages of the World Cup and the performances that followed or his ability to stand out in a midfield with Joao Neves and Vitinha is a testament to his place in this list.

As across 1,131 minutes in Ligue one this past season Ruiz maintained a 91.5 per cent passing accuracy rate, was in the 99th percentile for progressive passes completed and the 82nd percentile for both key passes and chances created to other midfielders.

These performances alongside his trophy haul for the season make the Spaniard an outside shout for the award.

Sports.title: Ben Stokes reveals reasons behind his shock retirement - and outlines his ambition to become England coach in the future
Sports.content:
Former England captain Ben Stokes has spoken publicly for the first time since his shock announcement about the decision to call time on his Test career.

Stokes, 35, shocked English cricket after announcing his retirement in June during the third and final Test against New Zealand.

It had been a series marred by drama with Stokes and team-mate Gus Atkinson missing the second Test after being dropped for breaking the team's curfew while out celebrating their first Test win at Lord's.

An incident in the early hours after that match saw an altercation at the Rex Rooms nightclub in Chelsea, when a member of the ECB’s security staff was struck by Saracens academy player Totoa Auvaa amid a disagreement over table arrangements in a VIP area.

Stokes eventually returned for the third Test but has now revealed his thought process behind his decision to call it a day.

'There's a lot to it that I think is just not for today or for the near future,' he told the Love of Cricket podcast.

'I look at planning ahead and I was going "We've got the Ashes in 2027" and I think you know I spoke to (wife) Clare a lot about this even before I took the decision.

'You always plan your retirement, right? And it was 2027 Ashes, whatever happens there you're going 'Not sure I go past that'.

Ben Stokes announced his shock retirement during the third Test against New Zealand at Trent Bridge

And then over time sort of I was (thinking) "How am I going to get there? How am I going to get to Australia 2027 with everything, with how everything is feeling at the moment?"

'Playing for Durham I'm going "How am I even going to get to end the New Zealand series?" I'm worrying about how I'm going to get there and thinking that Australia is going to be my last one.'

Stokes, however, remains keen to stay in the game. He is currently back playing for Durham in the One Day Cup and Daily Mail Sport reported this week he is in talks with Sydney Sixers over a Big Bash contract this winter.

Further down the line, though, Stokes revealed he has his sights set on taking the top England job.

'I'm doing my level three coaching now while I'm still playing because I want when the day comes that I'm not playing anymore,' he said.

'I'd love to be able to have all that stuff signed off and done. So then I've got that option if I want to go into it or I want to be, I have a couple years off and just do whatever I want to do.

'I want to be a coach. I know what I want to do in terms of staying within the game which is to be a coach. And would I love to be coach of England one day? Absolutely. I would love to be able to do that. Do I think it's going to happen? I don't know. No idea.'

Sports.title: UFC fighter, 34, found dead after 'apparent heart attack' in his sleep
Sports.content:
See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

UFC fighter Allan Nascimento has died at the age of 34 after suffering an 'apparent heart attack' in his sleep.

It comes just six weeks after the Brazilian's last fight in Las Vegas on June 20. He suffered a split decision loss to Mitch Raposo at UFC Vegas 119.

A UFC statement read: 'This morning, Monday, August 3rd, our beloved flyweight fighter, Allan Nascimento, was found unresponsive after suffering an apparent heart attack in his sleep.

'Despite the efforts of the responding medical team, he was pronounced deceased at the scene.

'Our thoughts and deepest condolences are with Allan's family, friends, teammates, and loved ones during this incredibly difficult time.'

The UFC's statement was accompanied by a single black-and-white photo of him smiling, while holding up his fist in a UFC boxing glove.

UFC star Allan Nascimento has died at the age of 34 after suffering an 'apparent heart attack'

It comes just six weeks after the Brazilian (left) lost last fight in Las Vegas on June 20

Nascimento finished his career with a 22-7 professional record, winning four of six UFC fights

Born in Sao Paulo, Nascimento built an impressive reputation by winning 17 of his first 22 fights.

A flyweight, the 'Puro Osso' - a Portuguese idiom meaning 'skin and bones' - competed in multiple promotions during his career, including RIZIN, Legacy FC and Dana White's Contender Series.

Nascimento then joined the UFC in 2021 and won four of his six fights. He finished his career with a 22-7 professional record.

He managed to secure the Performance of the Night bonuses for impressing fans in submission victories over Carlos Hernandez and Cody Durden.

Former UFC lightweight champion Charles Oliveira, who trained with Nascimento in Sao Paulo, posted an emotional tribute on social media.

He wrote in Portuguese: 'Today I lost a brother that the fight game gave me. Thank you for always being by my side, for sharing the mats and the corner.

'I have nothing but gratitude for having you with me - in training, in the corner, and just hanging out. I love you, man; you're a legend. My brother, I can’t even believe it; you will be deeply missed.'

Sports.title: What Morgan Gibbs-White's agent change means for Nottingham Forest future: Oliver Glasner's role, the boost for Bayern Munich, interest from Chelsea and where boyhood club Man United stand
Sports.content:
What Morgan Gibbs-White's agent change means for Nottingham Forest future: Oliver Glasner's role, the boost for Bayern Munich, interest from Chelsea and where boyhood club Man United stand

Unlock more from Tom Collomosse inside the Forest camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

The transfer news was announced across social media by a user with more than 100 million followers and designed for maximum exposure.

The player in question is Morgan Gibbs-White although – until now at least – he has not changed clubs this summer. Rather, the Nottingham Forest No10 has decided to switch representatives, from the powerful CAA Stellar to ROOF, an emerging force in the world of football agents, and the news came through football transfer influencer Fabrizio Romano.

ROOF's headquarters are in Germany and as well as Gibbs-White, they represent Kai Havertz, Virgil van Dijk, Ademola Lookman and Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler.

When players move to a new agency, the usual conclusion is that they are looking for a way out. While that is not necessarily the case with Gibbs-White, the move certainly raised eyebrows across the game, not least among the Forest hierarchy.

Here, Daily Mail Sport looks at where Forest and Gibbs-White stand and what might happen next.

When players move to a new agency, the usual conclusion is they are looking for a way out. While that is not necessarily the case with Gibbs-White, it raised eyebrows across the game

Gibbs-White (furthest left) is coming off the best season of his career, scoring 15 Premier League goals and 18 in all competitions

What is Forest’s stance?

Unless the offer is too attractive to turn down, Forest’s position is that they have no intention of selling Gibbs-White this summer.

With Elliot Anderson sold to Manchester City for £116million, there is little pressure on Forest to bring in cash from sales and owner Evangelos Marinakis does not want to let another star player go in the same window.

Having hired Oliver Glasner as coach, Marinakis’ plan is to improve, rather than simply consolidate. The idea is to build the new-look Forest around Gibbs-White, who missed out on a place in England’s World Cup squad despite 18 goals and seven assists in all competitions last season.

When Gibbs-White’s move to Tottenham last summer did not go through, he signed a new three-year deal at Forest, making him the highest-paid player in the club’s history. Forest’s plan then was to put Gibbs-White at the heart of everything and, after his brilliant 2025-26, they are not about to change tack.

They also believe Glasner’s arrival can take Gibbs-White’s game to another level – just as he did with Adam Wharton, Michael Olise and Eberechi Eze at Crystal Palace. But to achieve this, Glasner needs Gibbs-White to be fully committed, and not with one eye on a move.

Tottenham thought they had triggered Gibbs-White's release clause last summer. Forest thought otherwise and he signed a new contract

New Forest boss Oliver Glasner (right) was brilliant at turning players into stars at Crystal Palace, such as Michael Olise (left)

What is Gibbs-White’s mindset?

This summer and last, Gibbs-White has watched team-mates join Champions League clubs while he has stayed put. Last July, Anthony Elanga moved to Newcastle and this year it was Anderson’s turn to depart. Anderson, incidentally, is represented by Stellar.

This time a year ago, Tottenham believed they had activated a £60million release clause in Gibbs-White’s contract – but Forest thought otherwise and they won the day. Gibbs-White is very well compensated and is settled in Nottingham, where the Forest supporters adore him.

He would not be human, though, if the transfers of Anderson and Elanga had not affected his thinking. If they were good enough to play in the Champions League, Gibbs-White might have wondered, then why wasn’t he? While not necessarily unhappy at Forest, Gibbs-White is ambitious.

He was also bitterly disappointed to be left out by England boss Thomas Tuchel for this summer’s tournament despite turning in the best season of his career, scoring 15 Premier League goals to steer Forest away from relegation.

Daily Mail Sport can reveal that Chelsea showed a growing interest in Gibbs-White earlier this summer but the 26-year-old aspires to play as high as he can and that means the Champions League. He was a boyhood Manchester United fan who idolised Wayne Rooney, while at least once Manchester City have moved for him without taking the final step.

Indeed, Gibbs-White thought he was on his way to City in summer 2025, only for City to sign Rayan Cherki instead for half the cost of the England man's release clause.

As for United, it is thought their priorities currently lie elsewhere, with Bruno Fernandes producing a sensational campaign last term. Daily Mail Sport reported last February that Gibbs-White was seen as a potential replacement for Fernandes were he to leave United this summer but at this stage there appears little prospect of the Portuguese playmaker changing clubs.

This summer and last, Gibbs-White has watched team-mates such as Elliot Anderson (right) join Champions League clubs while he has stayed put

He was a boyhood Manchester United fan who idolised Wayne Rooney, while at least once Manchester City have moved for him without taking the final step

How will this play out?

It is understood that Glasner’s arrival has already had a positive impact on Gibbs-White. At the end of last season, with Forest finishing 16th and losing in the semi-finals of the Europa League, Gibbs-White was assessing his options.

Would he ever fulfil his Champions League dream by staying at Forest? In three of their four seasons since promotion, Forest have been fighting at the wrong end of the table. Last season they finished 16 points adrift of Liverpool, who claimed the final Champions League spot. That is a heck of a gap to bridge.

Gibbs-White is said to have been energised by Glasner’s arrival and has been particularly impressed with the Austrian during Forest’s recent training camp in Portugal. Gibbs-White will also be keeping a close eye on new signings. Will these, plus the arrival of a proven winner in the dugout, be enough to stop his head being turned?

Intriguingly, Daily Mail Sport understands that if Michael Olise leaves Bayern Munich this summer, Gibbs-White would be among the candidates to replace him. Olise is wanted by Real Madrid.

It is worth noting that ROOF have strong links with Bayern, who have recruited extremely well from the Premier League recently by signing Olise in 2024, and Harry Kane a year earlier. Historically, English clubs are more amenable to selling their top players overseas than to domestic rivals, which could also work in Bayern’s favour.

ROOF have strong links with Bayern Munich, who have recruited extremely well from the Premier League recently by signing Olise in 2024, and Harry Kane a year earlier

Gibbs-White is now at the centre of the Forest project and would expect to be treated as such

Saudi Pro League club Al Hilal are also seeking an attacking midfielder to play alongside former Wolves captain Ruben Neves, ex-West Ham winger Crysencio Summerville and 2022 Ballon d'Or winner Karim Benzema, yet it would be a huge step for Gibbs-White to move there in the prime of his career, and with his England dream still alive.

If Gibbs-White moves this summer, it may well be overseas. If he stays one more year, there would be other options – perhaps United, if this is to be Fernandes’ final season.

When Forest signed Gibbs-White for £25m plus add-ons after promotion in 2022, then-boss Steve Cooper assured him he would be properly backed even in periods of poor form, which had never happened at boyhood club Wolves.

He is now at the centre of the Forest project and whenever he moves, Gibbs-White will expect similar treatment. The next few weeks promise to be very interesting.

Sports.title: Alan Brazil announces return to talkSPORT after having life-saving operation
Sports.content:
Alan Brazil announces return to talkSPORT after having life-saving operation

Alan Brazil will return to the airwaves on the talkSPORT breakfast show this week following nearly four months off, spent recovering from a life-saving liver transplant

View 2 Images Alan Brazil announced his comeback in a video (Image: @alanbrazilts/Instagram)

Alan Brazil has announced his return to talkSPORT following a break after undergoing a live-saving operation. The 67-year-old broadcaster has been off the airwaves for nearly four months due to health problems.

‌



Brazil underwent a liver transplant, revealing in June that he was on the operating table for eight hours and that his heart stopped during the procedure.

‌



He has spent the past few months recuperating and now feels ready to return to his breakfast radio show this week. Speaking in a video of himself sitting alongside his dog in the sunshine, posted to social media on Monday, Brazil explained the plan.

‌



"I'm looking forward to Wednesday. Wednesday at 6am - talkSPORT, Brazil's back. Looking forward to it," he said. "I've had a great break here in Suffolk, the weather's been sensational although I'm not allowed to be in the sun too much. But it's been great.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"The World Cup - not so great for me. I didn't like all the commercialisation and of course we're hearing all about it now, aren't we?"

‌



After an interruption from his dog, Hugo, Brazil added: "Wednesday morning, it looks like Gabby [Agbonlahor] and me just after six o'clock, all being well I'll be back on. I'm going to have Thursday off because I've got a couple of treatments I've got to do, and then Friday I'll be back at six as well.

"Hopefully it'll be Ray Parlour - Party Parlour - I spoke to him yesterday and he was enjoying himself as normal. Some Sunday lunch in Essex, some swanky restaurant having a great time.

"I've missed all this, guys, over the last three months, I really have. And I've had a great break. I feel my voice and everything is beginning to improve week after week. I'm still not there yet, nowhere near - it'll take another three, four, maybe six months but I'm definitely a lot better.

‌



View 2 Images Alan Brazil is a talkSPORT stalwart (Image: TalkSPORT/ YouTube screengrab)

"I can't wait, I've taken some season tickets to Ipswich this year, so I'm going to spend a lot of time at Portman Road. Things are great."

In previous videos, the former Ipswich and Tottenham player described his operation and recovery as "a miracle", thanking the "brilliant" staff at Addenbrookes Hospital in Cambridge for saving his life. "I can't thank the people at Cambridge enough," he said.

‌



Brazil is a stalwart of talkSPORT, having presented the station's breakfast show since it launched in 2000. But his health deteriorated in 2026, with spells taken off the radio in January and March.

While he will work alongside former Aston Villa striker Agbonlahor and ex-Arsenal midfielder Parlour upon his return, Brazil said Scotland legend Ally McCoist was still taking a "well deserved" break following his work as a co-commentator at the World Cup with ITV.

UFC fighter Allan Nascimento has died in his sleep aged just 34.

The Brazilian flyweight, who fought six times for the UFC over a five-year period, was most recently in action in June when lost a decision to Mitch Raposi in Las Vegas. He had won four of his six fights with the promotion and held an MMA record of 22-7.

‌



A statement from the UFC read: This morning, our beloved fighter and exemplary flyweight, Allan Nascimento, was found unresponsive after suffering an apparent heart attack in his sleep. Despite the efforts of the responding medical team, he was pronounced deceased at the scene. Our thoughts and deepest condolences are with Allan's family, friends, teammates, and loved ones during this incredibly difficult time."

‌



Conor McGregor backed to fight again after latest injury setback READ MORE :

Tribues to Nascimento poured in with former lightweight champion, and fellow Brazilian, Charles Oliveira saying: "Today I lost a brother that the fight game gave me. Thank you for always being by my side, for sharing the mats and the corner."I have nothing but gratitude for having you with me in training, in the corner, and just hanging out. I love you, man; you're a legend."

The UFC itself added: : "A fixture on the doorstep of the Top 15, Nascimento was a constant presence alongside his team-mates whenever they made the walk, sharing an especially close bond with former lightweight champion and current BMF titleholder Charles Oliveira. Sports.title: Ben Stokes criticises Harry Brook captaincy snub and opens up on England drinking culture
Sports.content:
Ben Stokes criticises Harry Brook captaincy snub and opens up on England drinking culture

Ben Stokes has given his first interview since retiring as England Test captain, speaking about the decision to overlook Harry Brook as his successor and the alleged drinking culture around the team

View 3 Images Ben Stokes gave his first interview since his shock retirement (Image: For The Love of Cricket podcast)

Ben Stokes has questioned the decision to overlook Harry Brook for the England Test captaincy following his shock decision to retire. Stokes announced his retirement during the third Test against New Zealand at the end of June, plunging the team further into crisis.

‌



The England and Wales Cricket Board have since replaced Brendon McCullum with Stephen Fleming as Test coach, bringing to an end the Bazball era. Rather than hand the Test captaincy to Brook, who was Stokes' vice-captain, England cricket chief Rob Key opted to re-appoint Joe Root.

‌



Root led England for 64 Tests between 2017 and 2022 and stepped down after a run of one win in 17 matches. The 35-year-old is England's all-time leading run-scorer and is seen by Key as a safer pair of hands during this transition period ahead of a three-Test series against Pakistan later in August.

‌



Speaking to his former team-mates Stuart Broad and Jos Buttler on the For The Love Of Cricket podcast, Stokes held back from revealing all about his departure, but did question the logic of the captaincy succession. “If you think someone is going to be a good captain or a good leader, just give it to them,” Stokes said.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



“Brooky was made vice-captain. I’m not there any more, but even when I missed that Test match, I was like, ‘he’s vice captain?’ I sort of understood the reasoning why they were saying it, but I was still like 'what message is that sending to him?'

“He’s vice-captain, and the captain is not playing, but he’s not captain. And then the same again here. I had no leadership or captaincy experience when I took over. They just thought I was going to be a good captain."

Stokes retired not long after being dropped for the second Test against New Zealand following an incident in a London nightclub. While an ECB investigation found he did nothing wrong, with Gus Atkinson being attacked by a Saracens rugby player, the duo were both breaking the team's midnight curfew.

‌



View 3 Images Joe Root has replaced Ben Stokes as England Test captain after Harry Brook was overlooked (Image: Philip Brown/Getty Images)

The incident raised concerns about the team's relationship with alcohol after a shambolic Ashes tour in which headlines were made for the alleged drinking culture, and not long after Brook was fined for being punched by a bouncer in a drunken incident outside a Wellington nightclub.

Asked if the England team has a drinking problem, Stokes replied: "No, that's such an extreme thing to put on a team. I think cricket has a drinking culture and it hasn't changed. We're in 2026 now, where the game has got more professional over the years, and the one thing that has just stayed in cricket is its relationship with alcohol.

‌



View 3 Images Harry Brook did not succeed Ben Stokes as Test captain (Image: Gareth Copley/Getty Images)

"From club cricket and it works it way up, it's embedded in the sport. The relationship between alcohol and cricket is something that just hasn't moved on as cricket has become more professional, with sport science and medicine, nutrition.

"So, for the people who think that the English cricket team has a drinking culture, I'd say no, cricket has a culture that's associated with alcohol. I think it can be a problem... I don't know what you do to change it.

Article continues below

"I've had, I wouldn't say problems, but relationships with alcohol over my career that have been potentially dangerous, if that makes sense? But that's completely different to me now."

Sports.title: Arsenal may be using Vinicius Jr transfer talk as smokescreen for another huge deal
Sports.content:
Arsenal may be using Vinicius Jr transfer talk as smokescreen for another huge deal

Arsenal's chase of Vinicius Jr could pave the way for another marquee arrival in north London this summer

View 2 Images Vinicius Jr could be heading to the Premier League (Image: Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images)

Arsenal would be pulling off the biggest transfer in their history if they acquire Vinicius Jr from Real Madrid. However, their chase for the Brazilian star may not tell the full story of Mikel Arteta's transfer intentions.

‌



The Gunners' stunning interest in the 26-year-old was reported last week by The Athletic, who stated they'd be keen on signing him if he doesn't sign a new deal with the Spanish giants.

‌



Vinicius has just 12 months left on his contract and Madrid could be inclined to sell him this summer rather than let him leave for free next year. Even before the sale of Leandro Trossard to Besiktas, a marquee attacker was a priority for Arteta in his attempts to bolster their chances of defending their Premier League title this upcoming season.

‌



The Madrid superstar certainly fits the bill, but he isn't the only forward that Arsenal have had their eyes on this window. Yan Diomande has been a target for the north London outfit, with Liverpool, Paris Saint-Germain and Madrid all registering serious interest in signing the RB Leipzig left-winger.

While Vinicius is currently the superior player, Diomande, 19, is seven years younger than him and is equally adept at playing on both flanks. The Brazilian's contract situation could have played a role in Madrid moving forward in their attempts to sign the Ivorian, having launched an unsuccessful £85million bid for his services.

Vinicius Junior transfer: Arsenal ready to break salary record to sign Real Madrid star READ MORE :

Arsenal's two conditions for Bruno Guimaraes transfer as Gunners set to make next move READ MORE :

Arsenal's interest in Vinicius could be a calculated tactic to force Madrid to focus on extending his contract, which could result in the Gunners moving ahead of the pack in the race for Diomande.

‌



Talks may continue to loom over the Brazil international's future, but according to Diario AS, there is optimism that a deal can be reached to continue his eight-year tenure at the Santiago Bernabeu.

View 2 Images Yan Diomande is nearing a move to Real Madrid (Image: Hugo Rivera/Jam Media/Getty Images)

That optimism seems to have no bearing on their efforts to sign Diomande, with Sky Germany reporter Florian Plettenberg reporting that the winger has reached a 'verbal agreement' to join the La Liga side.

‌



However, the deal has hit a speed bump, with Leipzig managing director Marcel Schafer casting doubt on the progression of Diomande's move to Madrid. The German appeared to indirectly slam Fabrizio Romano for seemingly confirming Diomande's eventual sale on X.

The Italian had used his catchphrase 'Here We Go' when claiming an agreement between Leipzig and Madrid had been found in a deal worth over £85m for the Ivorian. Schafer unequivocally told Sky Germany: "It’s clear that some so-called transfer experts reported a few days ago that the deal was done or gave it the ‘here we go.’ That’s simply not the case. We’re not at that stage yet."

The update certainly gives credence to Arsenal's ability to usurp Madrid in acquiring Diomande. Just over a month remains in the transfer market and while they've added Christos Tzolis to their ranks following an impressive stint at Club Brugge, there's no doubt the opportunity to capture one of the leading attackers in world football will be a deal Arsenal chase until the window slams shut.

Sports.title: Ex-FIFA president was forced to resign and banned from football for 12 years
Sports.content:
Ex-FIFA president was forced to resign and banned from football for 12 years

Former FIFA president Sepp Blatter remains banned from the sport as his successor Gianni Infantino comes under pressure

View 2 Images Former FIFA president Sepp Blatter remains banned from football (Image: FABRICE COFFRINI/AFP via Getty Images)

Former FIFA president Sepp Blatter is still serving his ban from all football-related activities. The 90-year-old received two suspensions totalling more than 12 years, keeping him out of the sport until June 2028.

‌



In more recent times, Blatter’s successor Gianni Infantino has faced backlash after plans to sell stakes in FIFA competitions, including the World Cup, to private investors were revealed. The English Football Association is reportedly set to follow the Welsh FA in withdrawing support for Infantino’s re-election.

‌



European governing body UEFA recently said in a statement: "The current FIFA leadership has not only lost UEFA's confidence but also that of many other members of the football family.”

‌



While Infantino faces an uncertain future at FIFA, it is not the first time that the head of football’s world governing body has caused controversy. Blatter became head of FIFA in 1998 and remained in the role before being forced to resign in June 2015 after coming under investigation by the USA as part of a corruption inquiry.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

During a press conference, Blatter said: "My mandate does not appear to be supported by everybody." He was later given an eight-year ban from football in December 2015, alongside UEFA president Michel Platini, which was ultimately reduced to six years.

‌



Gianni Infantino was set to earn huge salary from World Cup plan as staggering figure revealed READ MORE :

The suspension related to alleged ethics breaches after Blatter made a £1.3million payment to Platini in 2011. Both parties argued the money was part of a verbal agreement for the latter’s work as a technical adviser between 1998 and 2002.

Both men, who always denied wrongdoing, were subsequently cleared of corruption charges in Swiss courts in 2025 in relation to the payment.

However that came some time after Blatter had already announced his plan to step away from FIFA and allow the governing body to find his replacement, with Infantino officially becoming his successor in February 2016.

‌



Blatter received a further suspension in March 2021. He was banned from the sport for another six years and eight months, upon the end of his initial suspension in October 2021, keeping him out of football until June 2028.

It was imposed following multiple breaches of FIFA's ethics code. The same length of suspension was also imposed on FIFA's former secretary general, Jerome Valcke.

The governing body found that Blatter received "an undue economic benefit" of 23m Swiss Francs (£18m) between 2010 and 2014.

‌



View 2 Images Blatter will remain suspended from all football-related activities until June 2028 (Image: Fabrice COFFRINI / AFP via Getty Images)

A Fifa statement said: "The investigations into Messrs Blatter and Valcke covered various charges, in particular concerning bonus payments in relation to Fifa competitions that were paid to top Fifa management officials, various amendments and extensions of employment contracts, as well as reimbursement by Fifa of private legal costs in the case of Mr Valcke."

The investigation also found that Blatter, Valcke, former Argentina football federation president Julio Grondona and ex-Fifa finance director Markus Kattner had “set up a scheme through which they were allowing themselves to obtain extraordinary benefits with a minimum of effort".

‌



The statement added: "This vicious circle saw three of them (Blatter, Grondona and Valcke) signing the amendment contracts of the others and approving the respective extraordinary bonuses, while the fourth (Kattner) was in charge of implementing the payment of such bonuses (as well as of keeping the matter ‘off the books’, by not reflecting the bonuses in the Fifa financial statements and not reporting them to the Fifa auditors)."

Blatter had begun working at FIFA as technical director in 1975, becoming general secretary in 1981. He was elected as FIFA president in 1998 and retained his position in four subsequent elections before resigning in 2015.

The 2021 FIFA Ethics Committee ruling said: “Mr Blatter held the highest position in football as FIFA president and, as such, had a tremendous responsibility to serve the football community as a role model. By his conduct, the integrity and objectivity of FIFA have therefore been exceedingly violated. FIFA’s reputation has doubtlessly incurred serious and long-lasting damage.”

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Bradley Barcola timeline emerges as Tottenham make their move for star
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Bradley Barcola timeline emerges as Tottenham make their move for star

Liverpool could be set to speed up their transfer business with their tour of the USA now coming to an end

View 3 Images Liverpool's interest in Bradley Barcola remains strong (Image: Getty Images)

Liverpool's need to dip into the transfer market has perhaps been exacerbated. The Reds wrapped up their pre-season tour of the USA on Sunday night with a chastening 4-2 defeat to Leeds United.

‌



The game was a Jekyll and Hyde-type performance from Andoni Iraola's side. Liverpool took a commanding 2-0 lead in the first half and looked in total control.

‌



Leeds then overpowered a much-changed Liverpool after the break and handed the Basque head coach his first defeat in charge. The aftermath has seen many fans across social media call for more recruits, with the Reds needing to address problems in defence and in attack before time runs out.

‌



Today's news sees the Bradley Barcola saga take a twist. Elsewhere, a Liverpool star has been targeted by Tottenham Hotspur.

Bradley Barcola timeline emerges

Fabrizio Romano has claimed that fresh contact will be made between the Reds and PSG this week. Speaking on his YouTube channel, he said, "new contacts [will be] prepared between Liverpool and Paris Saint-Germain."

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



4 transfers Liverpool need to complete after Leeds defeat showed harsh reality READ MORE :

Liverpool handed Bradley Barcola transfer boost as PSG strike contingency plan READ MORE :

Reports have stated that Barcola is keen on a move to Anfield, despite also being admired by the likes of Arsenal. Romando added that "conversations will continue next week", but claimed no deal is imminent, giving the Reds a longer timeline to get the deal over the line.

View 3 Images Bradley Barcola has been linked with Liverpool (Image: Franco Arland, Getty Images)

PSG are said to be looking for around £145m for the French international, but Liverpool are believed to want to bring that price down significantly. Romano said there is a possibility this transfer could run all summer, adding that it now "depends on Liverpool, on how much they want to spend."

‌



Spurs in for Cody Gakpo

Spurs are reportedly interested in Liverpool forward Cody Gakpo, but the Reds are reluctant to part with the Dutch star. Sky Sports claims Liverpool would be willing to let Gakpo go if they could source a replacement.

The Netherlands international also has four years left on his deal, and talkSPORT has suggested that Liverpool are likely to demand around £70m for the player.

Gakpo made 52 appearances for Liverpool last term, scoring nine goals and bagging six assists. However, if he were to depart, without a replacement being sought, it would leave Liverpool with only teenager Rio Ngumoha and new signing Victor Munoz on the flanks.

‌



View 3 Images Cody Gakpo of Liverpool (Image: Alex Pantling/Getty Images)

Spurs have splashed out £237m this summer and manager Roberto De Zerbi has hinted more is to come. "The transfer market, it's not finished for sure, but we completed 60 per cent of our project in the transfer market. Now we have another bomba!" he told football.london last week.

Gakpo moved to Liverpool in January 2023 from PSV Eindhoven for around £37m. He has made 180 appearances for Liverpool, scoring 50 goals and providing 23 assists, winning the Premier League in 2025.

Sports.title: Man Utd news: Marcus Rashford given fresh transfer option as club stance on striker emerges
Sports.content:
Man Utd news: Marcus Rashford given fresh transfer option as club stance on striker emerges

Manchester United continue to be linked with multiple deals during the transfer window as Marcus Rashford reportedly attracts attention from a new club

View 2 Images Manchester United star Marcus Rashford spent last season on loan at Barcelona (Image: Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Manchester United are nearing the start of the new season as the transfer window rumbles on. Michael Carrick’s side have brought in several new signings as the manager looks to improve his squad.

‌



Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos have been at the centre of United’s midfield rebuild following Casemiro’s departure to Inter Miami. Experienced goalkeeper Karl Darlow has also arrived at Old Trafford, alongside young shot-stopper Kit Margetson and attacking prospect Tynan Thompson.

‌



United have been linked with moves for several targets, including Arsenal’s Myles Lewis-Skelly and Newcastle full-back Lewis Hall. However, Marcus Rashford's future remains a topic of discussion after Barcelona’s decision not to sign the forward permanently.

‌



Meanwhile, United striker Benjamin Sesko is also claimed to have attracted interest from Bayern Munich. Here, Mirror Football looks at some of the biggest stories surrounding the club.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Marcus Rashford given fresh transfer option

Turkish giants Fenerbahce have reportedly made contact over a possible move for Marcus Rashford. The 28-year-old faces an uncertain future at United after Barcelona opted not to trigger their £26million buy option at the end of his loan spell.

‌



Man Utd transfer imminent as Michael Carrick greenlights rapid deal this weekend READ MORE :

Alejandro Garnacho takes brutal swipe at Chelsea immediately after Aston Villa debut READ MORE :

The Sun reports that Fenerbahce are prepared to “break the bank” for Rashford if the England international is prepared to join the club. It is claimed that the forward is one of three players on a shortlist, which also includes Crystal Palace's Ismaila Sarr and AC Milan's Rafael Leao.

It is reported that Fernerbahce have made contact with Rashford’s representatives to gauge his interest in joining the club. Rashford scored and assisted 14 goals apiece for Barcelona last season but the Catalan side decided to sign forwards Anthony Gordon and Karim Adeyemi this summer.

"What I can say about Marcus is I appreciate a lot to work with him,” Barcelona boss Hansi Flick said. "Sometimes it's not always that you do know what happens with players who are on loan. I think our situation is not easy for that.

‌



"But I appreciate working with him a lot; he's a fantastic player and a fantastic person. I think also the team miss him, I will miss him, but it's life, this is what we have to accept."

View 2 Images Benjamin Sesko has been linked with Bayern Munich (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Bayern Munich stance on Benjamin Sesko emerges

Bayern Munich reportedly remain interested in United striker Benjamin Sesko. The German side have previously considered a move for the forward and still view the 23-year-old as potentially part of the club’s long-term transfer plans.

‌



CFBayern Insider reports that Sesko continues to be a “very interesting” option for the club. Harry Kane currently leads the line for Bayern but it is claimed that the England captain could occupy a deeper role in the future, leaving space for another centre forward in the team.

Bayern have signed Ismael Saibari from PSV Eindhoven, reducing the need for another new striker. However, the report adds that Sesko remains on Bayern’s list of options. Sesko ended his debut season at United by scoring seven goals in 13 games under Carrick.

Sports.title: Arsenal news: Next Bruno Guimaraes bid imminent as Mikel Arteta message to target emerges
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Next Bruno Guimaraes bid imminent as Mikel Arteta message to target emerges

Arsenal are pushing hard to sign Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle

View 2 Images Arsenal have reportedly had a bid for Bruno Guimaraes rejected (Image: Getty )

After a slow and somewhat disappointing first half of the summer transfer window, Arsenal are ramping up their pursuit of several key targets. Since the Gunners’ Champions League final defeat to PSG in May, Mikel Arteta has repeatedly stressed the need to add quality signings, especially in forward positions.

‌



The Premier League champions’ underwhelming early business included announcing Piero Hincapie’s permanent move and signing third-choice goalkeeper Illan Meslier. They followed that up by replacing the recently-departed Leandro Trossard with £34million Greek winger Christos Tzolis, who grabbed a goal on his debut against Girona last Saturday.

‌



Arsenal’s first game of the 2026/27 campaign - a Community Shield clash with Manchester City on August 16 - will soon be in view as the season draws closer. As such, sporting director Andrea Berta is expected to push hard in the coming days to bring in a defender, a midfielder and a forward - which Arsenal hope will be Vinicius Junior.

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Now, Mirror Football takes a look at two of the latest transfer stories involving the Gunners.

Arsenal receive immediate response after finally submitting first Bruno Guimaraes offer READ MORE :

Mikel Arteta sends Vinicius Jr transfer message ahead of Real Madrid meeting READ MORE :

Second Bruno Guimaraes bid looms

Several reports claim that Newcastle United have rejected Arsenal’s first official offer for Bruno Guimaraes. The Gunners’ opening bid fell short of the £80m valuation the Magpies have placed on their captain and star midfielder.

‌



However, Arsenal are expected to return with an improved offer for the 28-year-old, whose contract expires in June 2028. Guimaraes has emerged as Arteta’s most pressing target in recent weeks and has reportedly already agreed personal terms with the north Londoners.

The Brazilian has also made Newcastle aware of his desire to leave, with the Emirates Stadium said to be his favoured destination. It is understood that Guimaraes is not willing to force an exit, however. Arsenal had floated a £45m verbal offer at the start of the transfer window but they were immediately shut down by the Magpies.

Arteta’s private message to target

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta is pushing to sign Vinicius Junior (Image: Getty )

‌



Arteta has reportedly taken charge of Arsenal’s pursuit of Vinicius by directly speaking to the Brazilian winger on the phone. The Gunners boss, according to Spanish outlet AS, has told Vinicius he will base the entire Arsenal project around the 26-year-old, should he join this summer.

It emerged last month that all key personnel at Arsenal had decided to pursue the Real Madrid forward, sanctioning the move in spite of the enormous cost of getting a deal over the line. Despite Vinicius’ contract expiring next summer, a fee of around £130m has been mooted in order to convince Los Blancos to part ways with the two-time Champions League winner.

Real Madrid remain determined to keep Vinicius but will look to sell him if he refuses to agree to a contract extension. They are reportedly unwilling to adjust their most recent contract offer to Vinicius and the club believes the decision now lies with the player.
